You had planned to work on your garden, but after light rain overnight, the garden is full of mushrooms attracting the insects to nest, so you need to destroy the insects to protect your beloved garden. Insects appear from the top of the screen and move across the screen, and if they hit a mushroom or the edge of the screen, then they move one place down and move in the opposite direction.

You cannot move through the mushrooms so you have to move around them and each mushroom takes a couple of hits from your gun to remove them. When an insect is hit then it leaves behind more mushrooms. Also on screen are butterflies and spiders with the butterflies moving around the screen while the spiders move down the screen leaving behind a trail of mushrooms. All insects and creatures must be avoided and if you touch one then you lose one of three lives. Once all insects are shot then you move to the next screen full of mushrooms once again.

170877.overview: You are a farmer and arriving at your field one morning you have discovered all your sheep have disappeared and they all must be found. In this text adventure you read descriptions of each location on the screen and you type in commands with the keyboard to control the farmer and interact with the locations.

170879.overview:
Magnetic Scrolls' last adventure before the introduction of their 'Magnetic Windows' format, Myth is classic interactive fiction.

Myth is set in Ancient Greece, place of myth and legend. Hence the title. You are are Poseidon, the Sea God. You have to journey to the Underworld to get the Dark Helment of Hades.

Its basically a tiny treasure hunt game where you get to play Poker with Charon and Death.

It is a very short game with a cunning puzzle or two.

170880.overview:
From the depths of the sea emerged the island of evil, and horror descended upon Vandor. the lovely planet - famous for its wines, its festivals.
The sun lost its light to the evil that now rules Vandor. Villages and towns are deserted, the once enticing forests are dangerous. Barren the valleys, forbidding the mountains, on whose slopes wine once fermented. When the night plunges the planet Vandor into black, one gathers in the stronghold and listens to the stories about the one who will set Vandor free again. So proclaimed Shandra the magician. But who dares to face the forces of darkness? Who is strong enough, clever and wise enough to interpret the few clues? Who dares enter the ice caves of Modra to find the king who left the land of Kruzia in grief and holds the key that could change everything?

Shandra the magician foresaw all of this. Nobody listened to him. - But Shandra is also the only one who still believes in rescue. No treasures beckon to the capable, the one longed for, no other reward than to bring Vandor back to freedom and to know: Evil can be conquered! Are you strong enough, friend? Then face the myth!

171553.overview:
Starlight #3. Find the keys to the doors and make your way out of the maze of twisty passages. 
 
You have been offered a wonderful job opportunity that you absolutely do not want to miss. But unfortunately, your arch enemy, having learned of the situation, has decided to prevent you from reaching your appointment on time. He tricked you into a spinning shuttle and locked you up in a maze. The only way to defeat your enemy will be to wander around your prison and try to reach the way out. Collect the keys to open the various doors and beware that some walls are illusory. But also remember that traps of various kinds are sown almost everywhere: some deadly, others to carry you from one part of the labyrinth to the other. Good luck! 
 
Published as Minotaurus in Italy's Videoteca Computer n.4.

171622.overview: The Lüsher Profile lets you look into your mind and personality by analyzing your preferences for various colors, shades and shapes. By recording and interpreting your responses to a variety of tests, a profile emerges of the factors which define your current approach to work, to relationships and to life in general.

171643.overview: Barney the Bellhop just heard the unfortunate news that his aunt Mabel has passed. To balance this, it seems Mabel has left her considerable fortune to Barney as an inheritance. Mabel has hidden her treasures throughout her 90 room mansion, and has created a series of traps and puzzles that Barney must solve to prove himself worthy of her fortune. His aunt furthermore has summoned various monsters from the netherworld in order to guard the mansion and thwart Barney's progression. Mabel's ghost continues to haunt the largest cache, and she must be evaded for Barney to claim his reward. The player must thoroughly explore the mansion, as keys have been cleverly hidden throughout the house. Various pieces of furniture must be pushed or manipulated, which will trigger events in other rooms. Weapons can be found hanging on the walls, and these can be used to vanquish the denizens of Mabel's domain. Each weapon is only effective against one monster. Barney can also jump, enter doors, and climb up and down staircases. The player starts with 15 health points, but loses points whenever they are injured. 0 points, and it's game over. To win the game, Barney must defeat all the monsters and collect every treasure in the mansion.

171645.overview: Macman: A single screen maze game viewed from above based on the arcade game Pac Man where you have to eat all the dots in the maze to move to the next level. As you eat the dots, there are three ghosts also moving around the maze and these have to be avoided because if you touch one then you lose one of three lives. In each corner are power-pills and when eaten allow you to eat the ghosts for a short period of time.

171646.overview: Mad Mission is a very simple split screen shooter and very simplistic alien attack waves (which seem to just repeat non-stop).  Graphically it is very simple. It was set to be published by Hewson, but may have never made it all the way to release with them. It was, however, published in Italy under several names including Son Guay or Son Gury in Hit Parade C64 n.39 (Novembre 1989) and Special Program n.56 (luglio/agosto 1989).

171647.overview: You're Ike Nash, a New York City cop waiting for a big break. That arrives when an inmate escapes from an asylum and the murders start piling up...

171670.overview:
A Maj-Jongg style tile removal game published in Game On 1991/08.

Developed by Twice Effects.

171671.overview: A basic platformer or maybe a platformer in BASIC. Seems you have to get all the green keys and use them at the exit at the bottom of the screen.

171672.overview: Would you like to talk about your problems? Eliza's pal Maggie would love to explore all your innermost thoughts and fears.

171673.overview: A horizontally scrolling shooter created by Karin Liebig and published in 64'er Sonderheft 66.

171674.overview: An Arkanoid style breakout game with baddies and power ups.

171693.overview:
Magic Duel is a 2013 two player only versus game developed by  Jörn Ruchmann in which both players play wizards. The winner is the one with the most successful attacks.in which both players play wizards. The winner is the one with the most successful attacks.

Released as part of RGCD C64 16KB Cartridge Game Development Competition 2013.

171694.overview: A game by Jens Döring & Johann Hartmut Stoeten to celebrate the 1988 Summer Olympics in Seoul, South Korea featuring swimming and various track and field events. Music was masterfully done by Markus Schneider.

171695.overview:
A puzzler with some nice music, the game was created by Cream Software and published in Magic Disk 64 1993/03. 

Magic Fields "is a puzzle game with 99 levels and a storable high score.

The aim of the game is to clear the playing field to remove all visible mussels free. If you press the fire button, so will all the surrounding fields
inverted in all four cardinal directions, whereby this process also includes the field under the hand. In this way, the whole playing field must now be cleaned. A level is only considered solved when no shell is visible any more. At the beginning you have three lives. As soon as the available time drops to zero, you lose a life and the timekeeper shows 999 again. With "RUN / STOP" the game can be stopped, but the screen will be cleared at the same time. This avoids the player cheating on additional thinking time. If you want to capitulate to this tough logic game, you just have to press "RESTORE" to get back to the main menu. After you have lost your last life, you can add yourself to the highscore list (or not!), Which is then immediately updated on disk.

171696.overview: A single player text adventure game created by Joseph Rezeau using the Quill adventure writer. You start with a simple discovery of something that catches your eye on the ground. It all gets weird from there.

171697.overview: A platformer by X-ample Architectures and published in Magic Disk 64 1992/07. Hello my little fellow, it is time to go and search for my magic book. I will give you some stars to defeat the Goblins of the Witch Anabel. Use them wisely my friend, and please hurry as time is against you.

171698.overview: Magic Duel: DoReCo Edition is a 2014 sequel to Jörn Ruchmann's 2013 game Magic Duel. The goal is the same. The game is 2 player only and you play rival wizards trying to take each other down. As in all other "duel" games of the same nature, the one with the most points is the winner after a set amount of points is reached.

171699.overview:
A Poker style game published in Magic Disk 64 1989/10. 

Wild West atmosphere, it's noon. Everything pushes from the dusty street into the saloon to have a cool drink in the hot temperatures. In the saloon, however, the atmosphere is more than tense: four men are sitting at a corner table, immersed in the cards they are holding in their hands. The motto is "poker", and in the middle of the table there is already a considerable pile green banknotes.

The mood turns icy when the four men at the table pick up the playing cards and sort them in their hands. No sound can be heard in the saloon, it is dead quiet. The four players attract everyone's attention, and everyone feels that there is something in the air. "I'll raise it by 50," grumbles the tall man with the scarred face and slides a corresponding note across the table. "Go with me and want to see ", his counterpart replies. The cards are turned over and lo and behold: both the scarred face and his opponent each hold four aces! !

The two opponents get up slowly, always keeping an eye on the other. Chairs are knocked over and those present hold their breath in tension. "You messed up, cheater!" Yells the scarred face, "and you will pay for it!" . In the same second the two cowboys hold two revolvers in their hands. Shots are fired, lead hisses through the air, and the smoke from the pistols drifts across the room.

Covered in blood, the cheater drops the pistol and sinks to the floor with a contorted face. But the scarred face was also fatally hit. Before he goes to hades, he stammers one last sentence:

"If only I had invested the 9 .80 DM in a new Magic Disk...!" . The bystanders just shake their heads uncomprehendingly at this sentence and turn back to their drinks. The computer gives you 5 cards and at the same time shows you all the winning opportunities in a box in the top right corner.
With the keys 1 to 5 you can now turn over the "superfluous" cards and thus release them for exchange. If you have particularly good cards in your hand, you can double your stake with SPACE (as long as you do not exceed the number 5!).
The second drawing is also started with RETURN . If you have won, you can RISK the number of points you have won.

171700.overview:
Magic Spells is an early educational program for multiple systems.

Designed to teach children age 6 - 10 basic spelling and grammar rules, in consists of a a series of three mini-games with animated graphics and sound. In each section, the player can choose words from a number of categories, including: animals, orchestra, fruit, and more.

Scramble Spells - The player is given a list of words, and the letters have been scrambled. The player must correctly unscramble each word.

Flash Spells - Words are displayed on the screen for a few seconds, and the player must memorize their spelling and correctly type them.

Players can create and modify their own set of words, and copy them to another disk to allow other players to participate.

171701.overview: A brain puzzle game where you are challenged to complete the magic square using numbers 1 to 9. In a magic square every row, column, and diagonal sum to the same number. The game was created by Hamar and Mitchell and released in 2010 by Falcon Soft.

171702.overview: Magic Squares is a sliding puzzle with 15 numbered tiles which must be shifted into the correct position is as little time as possible.

171703.overview:
Concentration and reasoning are two essential skills required to play Magic Tile\Duddo. IN practice, it is necessary to arrange all the available pieces on a chessboard in order to pass to the next level. The number of pieces remaining is indicated at the bottom of the screen and the piece to be placed at the the moment is indicated by an arrow. To position the pieces you must follow these criteria: They can only be placed next to other tiles of the same color or figure. If you can place a tile next to several tiles you will get bonus points. At the beginning you can select from various options including players, level of difficulty and saving and restoring games from disk. 

Published in Italy as Duddo in New Games Nuova serie n.6 (Febbrao 1993).

171704.overview:
It is your task to collect mushrooms. Unfortunately, this is not easy. Attacking bats, a snake and a female wizard, who is firing dangerous lightnings, are trying to stop you. It is also possible that one of the mushrooms is poisonous. If you manage to survive all these dangers enemies will get more difficult and dangerous. Enemies will even become, after some time with unpredictable breaks, invisible! To make your life a little bit easier, you will be warned with an acoustic signal and a flashing symbol.

The game is a fan translation of a German game called Zauberwald, which was done by the scene group, Antarctica on August 12, 2012.

171705.overview:
Hundreds of years ago when snails still dwelled in the Earth, Sonny the Snail lived happily with his parents in a place called Snail Meadow, and he was about to marry Dawny, his snailgirl of his dreams. All his happiness came to an end one day when troops of evil skeletons invaded Snail Meadow, robbed each house, killed their cattle, and kidnapped the snailwomen. After seeing Snail Meadow living in big sorrow, a wizardsnail decided to help them, but in order to do so, he needed several magic items - which include scrolls, mushrooms, money bags, and bag of coins - so that he can create his magical formula used to help track down the snailmates. He sends Sonny to collect these items.

While Sonny is busy collecting these items placed, he must deal with a wide variety of enemies - including enemy snails, green aliens, rotating skulls, balls, and bombs – by throwing slime at them. Furthermore, he must avoid the acid rain dripping from platforms. If Sonny comes into contact with any of the inhabitants or the acid rain, he loses one of his lives. When destroyed, some enemies leave behind certain power-ups that award Sonny with extra lives, time, or points. Occasionally, Sonny must destroy “huge enemies” including a cloud that throws lightning at him and two huge brains, and a skull named Freddy Snailcracker. Once Sonny has collected enough magical items, he proceeds to the next environment.

The culmination of the Sonny the Snail saga, a group of single-screen platformers created by Electric Brains Productions and New Entry with this one published in 64'er 1997/07.

171706.overview: A sample text adventure game of "AdventureWriter". You start the game to the south of a dark and foreboding castle near a sign that says to return with the Orb and the Scroll.

171707.overview: As Wuntvor, apprentice to the great magician Ebeneezum, who has disappeared, you must find and rescue him.

171723.overview: A 2D RPG Adventure game created in the style of Ultima by Ralf Prescher and Published in 64'er 1993/09. 15 years ago, the island of Aldora was conquered by the magician Tenomy and his horrific hordes of monsters. They were chosen by the inhabitants of Aldora. Destroy Tenomy You will be equipped with 1000 gold coins and 150 rations that will not last very long. Luckily for you, there are many villages on Aldora where you can calf. You can buy armor and rations. In order to be able to pay for all this, you have to fight Tenomy's monsters and capture their treasures. to open Tenomy's tower; to do this you need to find nine magic stones. The magician has hidden these in six dungeons or on the island and has them guarded by strong monsters.

171724.overview:
This strategical board game is flown between two players and it deals with tiles of two colors. In turns players place tile of their color on the 10x10 board, and if single tile of opposite color is between tiles of player's color, such tile changes it color and becomes player's tile. The goal of the game is to collect the number of your tiles greater than opponent's number until all board will be filled.

The game may be played versus computer or another player, but additional modes are available:

Demo Mode in C64 version, when computer plays against computer.

Published in Magic Disk 64 1993/11.

171736.overview: A mahjong tile removal game developed by Cameron Kaiser and published by Computer Workshops, Inc. in 1998. Now the classic combination of solitaire and Mah-Jongg returns with a whole new lease on life! MGSE is our upgrade to our 1993 smash hit. Match tiles and clear the board -- play against the clock or in our classic solitaire mode, all to a sumptuous Oriental soundtrack and great graphics. Can you meet the challenge of the Dragon?

171737.overview: A tile removing game published in 64'er 1993/01, and also in 64'er 1996/08. A game for relaxation, which guarantees you many hours on the breadbox and something for long winter evenings. Simply match the like tiles and make sure to allow the duplicate tiles pairs to allow later removal. After being removed, the game is ended when all pairs of tiles are removed.

171745.overview:
The Helios Exploration Starship is in for a surprise when it returns to Earth from deep space: alien invaders besiege the homeworld. 50 giant space fortresses orbit the planet, equipped with highly advanced Magnetic Force weapons. Humanity's only hope is the Helios' contingent of Photon Fighters.

Magnetron is a top-down action game consisting of 50 levels, each representing one enemy fortress. A fortress consists of a number of platforms in space. The goal in each level is to destroy all gun emplacements of the current fortress. Movement of the player's Photon Fighter is inertia-based - a thrust into a direction and the ship will continue drifting that way unless reverse thrust is applied. However, the ship won't necessarily drift indefinitely - the enemy's Magnetic Force weapons influence the craft as well and might divert the course, slow the ship or pull it in unwanted directions.

Each thrust of the engines deducts fuel from the tank. If fuel runs out, the ship is destroyed, but additional fuel can be picked up from tanks scattered over the platforms. The fighter can also employ an energy shield which prevents damage from enemy shots, but activating it drains fuel dramatically.

The platforms feature different kinds of walls: contact with solid walls destroys the ship, some others can be destroyed by laser fire, and special elastic walls reflect shots - in some levels the enemy guns can only be destroyed by a targeted reflected shot.

The game features a practice mode, which allows all but the last level of the game to be sampled. It also comes with a full level editor, allowing construction of complete sets of new levels. Walls, guns and fuel tanks can be freely placed, and the program also allows setting how the magnetic forces affect the player's ship. Levels can be saved to disk.

171746.overview: Puzzle game by John Fedor and published in the 1990 edition of Loadstar #070. This game will make you scream. Ever have the feeling that the world was slipping through your fingers, or that your sand castle was getting too big to manage? Well, step right up to Magnetron for another dose of frustration. This game will test your mind as well as your reflexes, as you scramble to keep the balls from slipping past you and falling outside of their intended bins.

171749.overview: A 2 to 4 player board game by Laze Ristoski for Ninja-Soft Technologies, that is in many ways similar to the game Sorry

171750.overview: A company management simulation developed by The Dark One, and published by The German Design Group. The German language version was published on "Commodore Disc #45"

171752.overview: A simple version of the complex turn-based strategy game played with small stones, seeds, beans or tokens and rows of holes or pits in the earth, a board or other playing surface. This version created by Bruce T. Robinson. The objective is usually to capture all or some set of the opponent's pieces and dates back to ancient Egypt or earlier.

171762.overview: Manganoid is an adult Arkanoid variant for up to two players. Regardless of the number of players there are two palettes available - one the top and left side. Removing cubes from the board reveals a manga style picture. All other Arkanoid rules apply, especially bonuses facilitating (two balls) or hindering (smaller pads) the task.

171763.overview: Your goal is to locate the mansion of your late uncle, then your legacy. Your uncle, who was somewhat eccentric, lived somewhere hear Upper Puddleton, but you're not sure of the exact location.

171764.overview: A game written by John Batchelor and released by Trash Productions in 1996. Fly over Canada and locate cities. You can race against another player or just test your own knowledge of Canadian Geography. You must pause right on your target.

171765.overview:
An educational computer game which teaches the locations and names of cities, towns, regions and rivers of Europe.

There are 3 modes, which are Opzoeken (Look up), Overhoring (Quiz), Het Stedenspel (The City Game). The game contains a mid 1980s map of Europe, as evidenced by countries such as East Germany, West Germany, Yugoslavia and Czechoslovakia. It contains many names and locations of cities, rivers and seas.

In Look Up mode you can type the name of a city or sea and the game will point it out on the map. In Quiz mode, the game will point a randomly selected place and the player must type in the name on time. The helicopter mode is the main part of the game. The player controls a helicopter and must fly to a randomly selected city or location before the time runs out. When the helicopter is close enough to the target city or location, it will turn into a pulsating red dot.

Additionally there is an information browser which shows data per country or a bar graph comparing all countries. The data includes the area in square kilometers, population, agriculture, industry and service industry data.

171766.overview: Radarsoft created the educational program Maps USA for the US market and it was distributed by ACK, Inc. Maps USA teaches people in the States the geography of their own country. There are three options to choose from, which are Search, Test and Heligame. In the Search mode the player can type in the names of the States, rivers, seas, mountains and the game will automatically go to the right place on the map. If there are several places with the similar name, then the computer will tell that the place was found, but will ask the player which one was meant. In the Test mode the player has to name the places that has been pointed out by the computer in a certain time. In the heligame player controls a helicopter and must fly within a certain time limit to find the places indicated by the computer. Each place that have been found you'll get points. If the points are high enough, the player will get extra time and lesser known places in the next level.

171767.overview:
Topografie Wereld is a Dutch educational program which was used in the '80s to help primary school children learn their geography of the world.

There are three options to choose from, which are Opzoeken (Look up), Overhoring (Quiz) and Helikopterspel (The Helicopter Game). The game use a mid 1980s map of the world, so there are countries that still exists in that time like the Soviet Union.

In the Look Up mode the player can type in places and the game will automatically go to the right place on the map. In the Quiz Mode the player has to name the places that has been pointed out by the computer in a certain time. In the Helicopter game player controls a helicopter and has to fly within a certain time limit to find the places around the world that have been indicated by the computer. These places will only appear if you are close enough. Each place that have been found you'll get points. If the points are high enough, the player will get extra time and smaller places in the next level.

171768.overview:
An Arkanoid/Breakout style game published in Magic Disk 64 1993/03. However in this game, instead of bricks, you have to take out a segmented snake/centipede-like creature in every level.

"Marble Springs" is not just any Arkanoid variant. No, it also brings the action aspect into play. There are not diverse, colorful stones romping about on the playing field, but a real dragon scurrying untiringly through the landscape. With bat and ball you must now hunt down this dangerous opponent.
If you move the joystick up or down, you can determine the energy portion of the ball. A great deal of sensitivity is required, because a strong charge of energy can cause great damage, but it also increases the speed of the ball. The ultimate goal is to find a balance between damage and control, because if the ball leaves the lower edge of the screen, it means the loss of a life.

When the score ends at "400" or "800", you automatically get a wider pad. Now the energy can safely be increased as the impact probability has improved significantly. The oversized pad only disappears as soon as you lose a life or get to the next level. In order to get hold of a ball that you thought was lost, you can press the fire button in addition to the direction of movement in order to accelerate the pad considerably.

171769.overview: You stole a space yacht and are drifting in pirate space, steering toward a pirate ship. Your objective is to locate the pirates' treasures and bring them to the utility room, locate the dymenthium ingots for your ship and bring them to the utility room, and discover what happened to the pirates.

171786.overview: A ROM hacked version of I Want More Diamonds with a Mario sprite and multilevels  created by AEG Soft.

171787.overview: The game is a Donkey Kong clone, with a beer machine replacing Donkey Kong.

171788.overview:
A multi event sports competition game published in Golden Disk 64 1991/06. here are over seven different disciplines to choose from. A game fun alone or with several. All graphics are drawn in detail, the animations of the fighters are perfect. With MARK-SET-GO you are right there, the real competitive atmosphere comes up when you play! A really gripping game in which you have to prove your skills in the individual disciplines and give your full effort. 

◉ 100M DASH
◉​ LONG JUMP
​◉ 400M DASH
◉ TRAINING CAMP
◉ BOXING
◉ GUN SHOOTING
◉ SHOOTING RANGE

171789.overview: A compilation of two text adventures: "The Museum Caper" and "Dial M for Marlo".

171792.overview: Part of the "4 in 1 Game Pack" and also the simply named "Game Pack". Land your rocket on the many landing pads on the surface of Mars using: Shift for main thrust, period to thrust right (and move left) and comma to thrust left (and move right). The border color indicates landing speed, green is safe to land. Bonus fuel will be given for successful landings. Watch out for Martians!

171795.overview: An Italian language action game from Giancarlo Castagna and published in CCC aka Commodore Computer Club, 22 (type-in) in 1983.

171796.overview:
Fly your plane over the city, watching Martian Pods drop from the sky. A tripod or a flying machine will hatch out from the crater left by the Pod. The tripods shoot at you and the flying machine will try to crash into you.  All the while a red weed starts growing and crawling. 

You must take out as many Martians as possible before your inevitable defeat. 
Published in both the Commodore 64 Games Book and the C+VG 1984/07 Book of Games.

171835.overview: To stumble into somebody else's computer system. To be someplace you're really not supposed to be. And to get the strange feeling that it really does matter. "LOGON PLEASE:" is all you get to start with. That's it. From there, it's up to you. If you're clever enough and smart enough you could discover a world you've never before experienced on your computer.

171838.overview: Master Head is a variant of Soko-Ban. On each level, the player, as a warehouse keeper, must push around crates to get them onto the right spots. Once all crates are moved onto a marked spot, the level is complete. Crates can only be pushed one at a time and cannot be pulled. A single wrong move can be undone with the P key. If the player gets stuck, it is possible to restart the level, but it causes the player to lose a life.

171839.overview: A game based on the code-breaking board game of the same name or the earlier pen and paper Bulls and Cows game. Published in Game On 1992/04.

171840.overview: A nice game of Codebreaker\Mastermind. Was also published in CBM Public Domain - Games II

171842.overview: Computerized version of the popular code breaking puzzle/board game developed by Zong Hoa Matthias Dörge in 1988.

171844.overview: An educational quiz focused on the hardware and technology of the day.

171848.overview: A version of Codebreaker published in The Netherlands having 4 levels of difficulty.

171849.overview: From the book "100 Programs for the Commodore 64", MasterMind is a computer implementation of the board game of the same name by Ian McLean and John Gordon  . The single player must crack a code of four digits and after each guess is given clues in the form of "amount of digits that are correct" and "amounts of digits that are correct but not in the right position". The goal is to guess the code in as little guesses as possible using logical deduction.

171851.overview: A mastermind strategy board game published in the book "29 Programs for the Commodore 64/264". This was also released a year later in Germany under the name Mamco, and published by Ing. W. Hofacker GmbH in the German translation of the same book, which was titled.  "Mehr als 29 Programme für den Commodore 64".

171853.overview: A homebrew version of Codebreaker\Mastermind put out by Ray Winter and "Winterware" and released to public domain.

171856.overview: Test your code-cracking prowess with Mastermind, the challenging game of logic and deduction. Your compy sets a secret code, and you, the Codebreaker, try to match the code using logic, deduction, and maybe even a little bit of luck. After each move, the game gives clues to the Codebreaker for you to try again. Published in UpTime Vol.1 #07.

171857.overview: A version of Codebreaker that was published as part of the "Leisure Time Classics" game pack.

171858.overview: In this game by Zodiac Mindwork and released in 1991 in Magic Disk 64 1991/05. Guessing numbers to the point of madness in this code breaking game.

171859.overview: A logic based Board game created by Martijn Tonies and published in Game On 1995/02. In this game the computer secretly puts four dots behind the shield. It will use any combination of 4-9 colors depending on the difficulty you choose. It can use dots of the same color. Its up to you to try to duplicate the exact secret code. Each time you guess a row of colors the computer will tell you which dot is wrong, right or right but in the wrong place. You can then try again. The winner is the one which guesses the code as fast as possible in the least amount of tries.

171860.overview: Mastermind or Master Mind is a code-breaking game for two players. The modern game with pegs was invented in 1970 by Mordecai Meirowitz, an Israeli postmaster and telecommunications expert. It resembles an earlier pencil and paper game called Bulls and Cows that may date back a century or more. This version was published on the Reset #09.5 Mix-i-Disk and in Reset 64 magazine 9.5.

171861.overview: Match Wits is a memory/concentration game mixed with elements from quiz and word guessing games. The game is for two players who take turns turning over squares to reveal the hidden words. The aim is to pick pairs of matching words which are then removed from the board. As squares are removed a hidden picture puzzle begins to be revealed and the players get chances to guess on its meaning. The player that enters the correct answer will win the round. A game consists of three rounds and the player with the highest score wins. There are six different subject categories to choose from: animals, cities, multiplication, words, sports and famous people. The game also comes with a secretary program that allows the player to edit and add content to the game.

171862.overview: A type-in number based puzzle game published by Fontana Paperbacks in the book "Giant Book of Games for Your Commodore 64". The game is similar to other early games of the same type, such as Matches.

171863.overview: A brain logic game created by Mark Tuttle and published in the "The Big 100" collection.

171864.overview: A logic\puzzle game published in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/11 (Issue #41). If you like puzzles, try your hand at one of the five variations of this entertaining solitaire game. "Match Blox" is a solitaire puzzle game in which you try to solve any of the five variations in the fewest number of moves possible. Each game is played on a 3 X 3 matrix of squares, and each square is colored blue or orange. The object is simple: Manipulate the squares until they match the pattern displayed.

171914.overview: After all your training you now face your final test to receive the title of Matchmaker and it involves getting a Prince and Princess to the church to get married. Other tasks are to make sure they are dressed for the occasion and to get a correctly dressed page boy as well. You have to move around your village and surrounding areas entering buildings and shops to interact with people who will give tasks to receive the items you need. Match Maker is a text adventure where you read text on the screen which describes each location and you type in commands to control your hero and interact with various locations.

171915.overview: Matchmaker US Geography is a new curriculum-based learning program that has been teacher designed to develop and strengthen knowledge of geographic facts. It will support most US geography courses taught in schools. The program is versatile and easy to use. It requires no previous computer background. Matchmaker US Geography works on the principle of matching words and phrases. It is excellent for expanding and reinforcing factual knowledge of US geography. Matchmaker US Geography also has a unique authoring feature which lets you create your own programs, quizzes and games simply by typing your entries on the computer keyboard.

171916.overview: Solve math problems to get rid the alien threat. This game was developed by Dean Hodgson and published by Pyramid Software in 1983.

171917.overview:
Stop the "bombs" that come in the form of math problems before they hit the ground and explode. This game was developed by Dan Dickerman and published in the following:


-   COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1986/10 (Issue #40)
-   COMPUTE!'s Commodore 64/128 Collection - Volume 2.

171942.overview: Math Busters is a math game that comes in the guise of an adventure game. This game was developed by Tom Snyder Productions and published by Spinnaker Software Corporation in 1984.

171944.overview: An educational math game that was part of "Math Magic" collection. Fun and math would be an oxymoron in any other case, but not in the case of this brilliant adventure game. This game ensures that you really have to think, whether you're evading and shooting demons or solving a tough problem.

171945.overview: An educational math game that was part of "Let's Count" collection. Let's Count helps young children of 4 years and above with early numerical skills for the numbers 0 to 9. Maths Muscles is in the fair ground and he has to ring the bells in ascending number order.

171946.overview: Be fast and accurate and you'll live another day in Math Tombstone. An educational game released in 1980 by Micro-Ed. The idea of Math Shootout is to practice doing math exercises as fast as you can. If you are swift enough you can beat Bad Math Mac who is out to get you.

171947.overview: Mathbooster is an educational game that masquerades as a Space Invaders type shooter. It was developed by Dean Hodgson and published by Australian based Satchel Software in 1985. Math Booster allows students to improve math skills by planing an exciting arcade-style game. Practice addition, subtraction, multiplication and division. The nature and difficulty of problems are easily adjusted to the individual student's needs.

171949.overview: This Maths test is a collection of multiple choice questions designed to exercise the student who is preparing for G.C.E. examinations.

171950.overview: A straight forward set of math questions in a game created by Bill Dyck and released in 1983.

171951.overview: In Matrix you can find word and word sets in the Byoggle-like matrix of letters and score them in this game from James Speers, for one to 6 players. It was originally released in UpTime Vol.1 #09  a monthly disk magazine for the c64/128 featuring programs, tutorials, articles and reviews. The object of the game is to find as many 4-letter or longer words as you can in a 5x5 maze of random letters within a set time limit. The game is competitive with each player using the same maze and time. Score is higher for longer words, and ONLY words not used by any other players will be scored. The letter Q in the maze works as Qu to make things easier. You may start with any letter and each letter in the word must adjoin the previous one horizontally diagonally or vertically. No letter may be used twice in the same word. Plurals, past tense, etc are all counted as separate words.

171952.overview: A single player, fantasy themed text adventure released in 1995 by Logyk Software.

171953.overview: Matt Lucas is a classic text adventure with static graphics, created using the Graphics Adventure Creator (GAC). The game puts you in the shoes of the eponymous private investigator in the state of Florida where your partner John Harpinger has just been kidnapped. You need to pick up on and follow the clues along the way while infiltrating the underground to track down your partner.

171956.overview: For ages 4 to 8. A truly superb educational game which makes addition and subtraction fun and addictive.

171975.overview: Maxi Maze is a very simple and short 1-player maze escape game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by General Masters Corporation and published by ALA Software in 1983.

171978.overview: A two player overhead car racing game created by  Holger Höller and Martin Hoffmann and released in 1995.

171982.overview: A 1988 game demo with this included game created by Steen Pedersen & Gandalf/Ikari, graphics by Brian K. Hansen and music by  Barry Leitch, Thomas Egeskov Petersen & Jens-Christian Huus. The game was a horizontally scrolling space shooter.

171984.overview: A Shoot'em-Up Construction Kit built game by Champion Software and Seuckers as a collab.

172005.overview:
An a-mazing maze game. Commodore Computing International v02-03 (Jul 1983) / from the book "CBM 64 Programs - Volume 1". Maze is a highly amusing and intricate journey through randomly created mazes in three different levels of complexity. The player is offered a choice of maze level and asked whether he wishes to see the maze being created. If the player opts for a maze without seeing its creation then he must be prepared to wait for a moment, until, with a flourish, the concocted maze appears. This game makes use of the four function keys on the right hand side of the 64. To manipulate the cursor through the maze, the keys' values are as follows:
f1 =up
f3 = left
f5= right
fl = down
The player is timed against a seconds clock in the top left hand corner of the screen. A fast time for one of the small mazes is 26 seconds.

172006.overview: Depredators Design put out this maze action game in both German and English in 1991. You have to eat the stars to get energy. If you leave the maze through an exit you must have one more energy point than your level. If you touch a well you simply lose one energy point.

172007.overview:
This is a game I created for the Commodore 64 using the cc65 C cross compiler toolset.  I wrote it in just a few days.  I asked my son to describe a game to me that I should make, and this is more or less what he described.  Of course, he had in mind something modern in 3D but I wanted to make it in less than a week and for the Commodore 64. 
 
You play as secret agent Mr. White. Your mission is to collect all the intelligence dots. Dot get caught by the guards. Shoot guards only when you have no other choice. Use boosts to outrun the guards when possible. You get one point per microdot, 10 points for unused boosts and 100 point for every unused bullet. 

2 Play modes. Survival where you have no gun and Escape where you have a gun but there are less escape routes.

172009.overview:
A game from the notorious Cassette 50. It has the distinction of being the first game on every version of the Cassette 50 compilation with the sole exception of the ZX Spectrum release. 

In this Pac-Man inspired game, you play the titular Pac-Man like character and have to eat all the dots in the maze while avoiding the ghost (there's only one) within the maze.

172011.overview: Try to get out of the maze as quickly as possible.

172012.overview: A fantasy text adventure based on Nogard, but with PETSCII graphics added. Your king is at war and as an elite Nogard warrior you have been chosen to bring six items to him as he hides in his storeroom under a bed. You have only your official Nogard Warrior surplus Warlord Battlepack (a plastic bag), a newspaper and a pair of clean undies!

172043.overview: A shooter created by Champion Software using Chris Yates' Shoot 'Em Up Construction Set.

172045.overview: A Worm/Snake style game developed by Neodyne Projectsm and first published in Game On 1993/06.

172049.overview:
An action game from Bob Carr of Magic Carpet Software, released in 1982. The medicine man has overdone it again, and the village is threatened by flood. In panic the elders call upon 'Copecoee' the ancient god of energy. Control Copecoee with the CRS control keys. (lower right corner of key board)
Release his energy rays with the shift key scoring 10 points for each rain drop you destroy and 20 points for each snowflake.

172090.overview: Medieval Mayhem is a Medieval themed vertical scrolling shooter developed by Christian Siege using Chris Yates' Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit.

172091.overview: A sword and sorcery text only adventure created by Matthew E. Kagemann and released by Magimax. in 1988.

172092.overview: A one or two player Shoot'em up dueling game created by Paul Kubiszyn & Jonathan Hunt )of XL.C.US Software and published in Commodore Format 1995/01 (Issue #52).

172093.overview: A multi-genre game primarily a shooter consisting of 4 levels\gates.  The first gate called Fight in Space is pure shooter. The second, Space Harbor, you must choose three of the correct add-ons to progress (the wrong ones will end the game). Space Harbor Deeper Rooms is an insanely-long snake game. Ultimate Fight is a safe-cracking game which seems impossible because the code could be anything! First published in Game On 1990/02.

172094.overview: A Pong style head-to-head game developed by Richard Bayliss, and released in GO64! 2003/02, and once again in GO64! 2004/02. The game was also released on Bayliss' TND website.

172095.overview: A twist on a Space Invaders type game, except with power ups and boss levels. First published in Golden Disk 64 1993/03.

172154.overview: Danish language game in which you control a rocket and must avoid a meteor falling toward you. This game was developed by Carsten W. Kock and published by NY Elektronik ApS in SOFT Special #85/3 (May/June 1985)

172185.overview: An arcade style avoid-it game created by David and Richard Darling and released as a sample of "The Games Creator", teaching game creation concepts.

172188.overview: A faithful remake of Megamania for the C64 released for fun at Visionparty 2002. You control a spaceship at the bottom of the screen and need to defend yourself from numerous waves of attackers. But in this game, like in MegaMania, the attackers are much more bizarre than invading aliens. There are hamburgers, diamonds, steam irons, bow ties, space dice, and more! You need to earn points by destroying as many of these strange attackers as you can before your energy supply becomes depleted.

172189.overview: The 2002 Minigame Competition's challenge was to make a worthy C64 game in 1K or less, this is Lubber\Padua aka Marco Wienkoop's attempt at such a game, based on the classic 2600 game that seemed so ahead of it's time. Eventually a bigger and much improved full game version would be released at Visionparty 2002.

172191.overview: Get on the saddle of your Megabike and blast your way through anything that gets in your way in this shooter from Arnd Bichoff released in 1984.

172192.overview: A brain memory game from Wojtek Wrona, Radek Andrzejewicz and Scatman, released by Cybertech Laboratories in 1996.

172193.overview: A simple platform game first published as part of Game On 1990/04.

172194.overview: This board game by John Patrick Green is keyboard controlled. Each space on the board is lettered from A to X, starting left to right, top to bottom. Start off by placing your characters by typing the letter of the spot you want to start it on. If you wanted to start playing the game and if you wanted to move the character standing on the top left, to the right you would press A followed by B.

172195.overview: A single player 2k Worm\Snake game by Charles Grey aka Iceout Games.

172196.overview:
Memologie is a simple puzzle-solving game. The goal requires finding all the covered pairs of pictures on the 6x6 board. Discovered pairs stays on the board with the mark 'ok'. There is a moves limit, indicated by the counter on the bottom panel. 

Developed by Keen Acid and published in Game On 1995/07.

172197.overview: Memomania is a simple puzzle-solving game. The goal requires finding all the covered pairs of pictures on the board. Discovered pairs disappear from the board. There is no time, counter on the top left corner indicates how many mistakes may be done. This game was originally created in another language, the original language version is still missing.

172198.overview:
A brain/memory game. Here is a puzzle unsuitable for those who have a photographic memory, but it could be used to develop everyone else's memory. In practice, it is a question of observing a screen with 25 sets of matching icons that appear uncovered for 10 seconds and then finding all the matches in the set time frame. 

Published in Italy as Memoteca in Special C64 n.5 (1991/1992).

172232.overview: A Brain\Memory puzzle and improved sequel to the original Memorix game.

172233.overview: You awake slowly to bright lights. You are feeling confused as you look around the room. You cannot remember how you got here. As you begin to awaken you realize that you are tied down to the bed! As your eyes begin to focus you see a TV on the wall. It appears as if you're in a hospital room. Who are you, why are you here and can you escape?

172234.overview:
Memory Building Blocks is a tile matching memory puzzle game.

Designed for young children, players take turns matching shapes, colors, words, tunes, and pictures. There are a variety of board designs, and allows for one or two players. A score or each player is displayed when all tiles are flipped.

172235.overview: Memory Castle is an educational game where the player is a knight who has to enter and accomplish tasks in a castle. The game gives instructions to the player who has to memorize them. The player is then asked questions on what should be done next, for example where to go, and has to answer correctly to progress through the game. An incorrect answer leads to the game ending. The game has three difficulty levels which differ in number of tasks: easy (6 instructions), medium (12 instructions) and difficult (20 instructions). Upon completion a reward is given which is different for each level.

172236.overview: A memory game that can be played with a  Joystick or with a Lightpen\Stylus. It has two game modes: find pairs of numbers or pairs of shapes. Created by Alakran aka Santiago Cárdenas and released in 2013.

172237.overview: A three part strategy detective adventure.

172238.overview:
Mental Blocks consists of three games:
Free Fall, or Fits and Pieces, is a 3D version of Tetris. Instead of forming a line, you must form a complete layer before it will disappear.
The California Achievement Cubes, or Mental Detector, shows you a cube, and challenges you to figure out which of the four unfolded cubes matches the cube. The single-player version has a timer, while the two player version has you pick the proper cube first.
What's Next, Pussycat?, or Shapes Happen, shows you three shapes, and asks you to pick the next shape in the series from a set of four choices. Again, you either face the timer or your friend.

172244.overview:
Play and sing the Fisher-Price way with this colorful and very grand piano. Your mom can't say that THIS is an outside toy! Now you can play over thirty different songs without reading a note of music! Just listen to a song. Then play each note along with the computer and listen as the computer plays it back to you. That's making music! When you get really good and can play all the tunes you've learned, you can even make up your own.
Based on the popular Fisher-Price toy, My Grand Piano brings the enjoyment of music to young children of all ages. It's an easy and entertaining introduction to the theory of the piano and the classic songs of childhood - it's also a terrific way for the novice player to build confidence at the computer keyboard!

172288.overview: Published in Game On 1989/11. This Uridium style shooter would be modified significantly and re-released as Counter Force.

172290.overview:
After the exhaustion of most energy resources, the existence of the epsilon dimension was discovered, from which waves of pure energy seemed to be coming. Foster prepared his spherosorb craft and explored through the wormhole into the epsilon dimension. With extreme surprise, Foster realized that this strange world with a radial structure was made up of variously colored sectors, some of which are inter, but others rich in energy. Additionally, there were regions dangerously capable of absorbing the energy of the spherosorb. By carefully adjusting the screens and avoiding the clash with the strange inhabitants, Foster found he had to touch the colored sectors to understand their nature. 

Published in Italy as Stripe in Special Program n.37 (novembre 1987) and Hit Parade C64 n.22 (Aprile 1988).

172320.overview: How long can you avoid the heavenly threats that barrage you?

172321.overview: A cross-hairs shoot'em-up game where you protect your ship from the meteor shower.

172322.overview: In this game published in Game On 1993/01, you are a silver orb and must maneuver around a twisting labyrinth collecting puzzle pieces and shooting and avoiding enemies, using the teleporters and using the floor triggers to open parts of the maze to explore, but be quick or time will run out.

172327.overview: The player must navigate their space ship and destroy everything in space, including mines, cruisers, and star bases. (The cruisers are only visible when you approach their base. They then approach your ship and start circling it, urging you to wipe them out.) Two types of rocks can be found. Red rocks contain minerals which increase your score when they are collected. The player needs to destroy these rocks quickly before it is replaced by a processor. Green rocks leave behind smart bombs that can be used to destroy the star bases, but only three smart bombs can be used at a time. The game ends when the player runs out of energy or goes off the edge of the playfield.

172330.overview: Metropolis is a flick-screen platformer with some puzzle elements. Most screens have enemies following a straight path. Navigate through the screens and avoid touching any enemy, since that drains your energy. Find and collect items for later use. You can jump and open doors. At first, you control the main character Moonboots the Lunar Explorer, who is stranded in Metropolis and must find his spaceship and refuel it to return to his home on the moon. During the game, Moonboots can change into three companions when carrying the right objects. They are Zoid the Droid, who is short enough to go under certain obstacles, Super Spy, and the Mad Monk. Some areas of the town are accessible to certain characters only, and some passages can only be traversed when you carry the right object.

172333.overview: Two of the greatest icons of the Golden Age of the NBA match up in this game. On one side, the spectacular dunks of Michael Jordan of the Chicago Bulls; on the other, Larry Bird's incredible accuracy from the outside. While Bird feels right home at the three-point contest, where five racks with five balls each are placed around the three-point arc and the player must pick each ball and throw in the the best timing possible to get as many points as possible during the 60 second window, only Jordan has the air-time to perform on the slam dunk contest, where the player has a number of dunks at his disposal, each requiring different timing to get the best score from all three attempts from the judges, and win the competition. While they are two completely different players, they can still go one-on-one on a half-court match, played to points or with a time duration. Can Bird's stealing and outside shooting ability be a match to Jordan's speed and jumping abilities?

172334.overview:
Drive a car to compete in the great Island Treasure Hunt.

"Featuring 'Instagrafiks' (Instant full colour resolution graphics!)... Only the best drivers need apply!"

172335.overview: Micro Painter was originally offered as a tape loader game, a simple game that you could play while your primary game was busy loading.

172336.overview:
This was a "tape loader game" which was a very small game that could be loaded into memory and played while you waited for the main game on the tape to load. Commodore tape load times could be close to 30 minutes in some cases. The object of the game is to rescue six stranded men from the surface of the planet and return them to the mother ship before the main game has loaded.

The game was a clone of Taito's Lunar Rescue.

172337.overview: the first version of Microchess was published in 1977 for various CP/M and Z80 machines and was ported to the Commodore PET/CBM a year later. So the first version of PETChess for the C64 was pretty much ready to run even before the machine debuted. This updated game is a graphically improved, and faster version of that first port and it does a pretty good job, without too many slowdown, especially when run from floppy.

172339.overview: Microleague eschew action in favor of strategy for this licensed baseball game. The real-life teams and players are included, as well as classic teams from the past - lots of data disks were released featuring additional lineups. Each play is graphically shown, with a running commentary detailing how it unfolds. A wide range of strategies are available. You can bring the stand-in players in, and instruct players as to how aggressively to play when opportunities arise, with 7 distinct batting strategies. When fielding you have options on field placement and bowling style - use the fastball and curveball wisely. Players will sometimes pick up injuries (the correct level of warming up can reduce this risk), or argue with the umpire over controversial decisions.

172362.overview: An add on to the primary game that allows box scores to compiled automatically for the teams you store for the entire season of play with other MicroLeague teams. See your whole season's stats all in one place and print them out to review later.

172363.overview:
If you've wanted to play the multi user game Multi User Dungeon but didn't have a modem then here is your chance. The game plays like the original except instead of human players the computer creates and plays as the humans. The aim of the game is to become a wizard by scoring 102400 points. This is done by killing other players, performing minor tasks or collecting treasure. To save your treasure you must put it in the swamp.

There are over 400 locations with a database of 100 characters but only 10 play at a time. Watch out though, there are 112 baddies out there to make things harder. With only 250 treasures to locate and collect by 10 players, the treasure soon goes so the game resets. Any treasure you do not have in the swamp is lost forever.

The game is played in the style of a text-adventure with no graphics. Putting in commands directs your character who can interact with the other players. The game is played in real-time as you watch characters come and go in one location.

172366.overview: Platform/collect em up game with a similar look to Henry's House. Released in 1985. Developed by Roger Svensson for Arcade System, and published by Computer Boss International

172370.overview: Midway Campaign is a computer simulation of the Battle of Midway Island in June 1942, arguably one of the most decisive battles in the history of warfare. The computer controls a huge force of Japanese ships whose objective is to invade and capture Midway Island. You command the badly outnumbered and outraged American forces with your only advantage being the element of surprise. The game ends if either all of one side's Aircraft Carriers are sunk, or any part of Japanese TF exits map to west or US TF exits map to east with no airstrikes in the air. At the end of the game a summary of all carrier damage, aircraft losses, and victory points from other targets and the Midway invasion are output followed by an evaluation of results.

172371.overview: Miecze Valdgira II: Władca Gór is an action-adventure game. This time king Aldir must defeat Bloody Zenon, that uses Cyclops eye to terrorize the surrounding area. Aldir must wander the surrounding forest and underground labyrinth, collecting one-use items along the way and using them in the right places, mostly to open underground passages. Each location is inhabited by hostile creatures. Contact with the creatures for longer than two seconds means instant death. The best way to circumvent the enemy is jumping over or passing under them.

172372.overview: Take the Mikoyan-Gurevich MiG-19, a Soviet second generation, single-seat, twin jet-engined fighter aircraft, the world's first mass-produced supersonic aircraft out for a spin. Dodge the fighters coming at you, the tanks shooting at you and make it safely back to the tarmac.

172374.overview: Odd little platformer made in BASIC released by Klaus-Dieter Frohn and published in both 64'er Sonderheft 66, and in 64'er 1999/01. Mike the Caveman: An archaeologist is desperately looking for the exit from the old pyramid before he runs out of air. Find the right path away and save Mike! The archaeologist Dr. Mike Holehead has himself trapped in the catacombs of the Chenon Pyramid. Help him get back to daylight!

172389.overview: A two-player only betting/gambling game where you will only have virtual losses. Music by Thomas Bendt & Mario Kriwanek.

172390.overview: The Milky Weigh is an action game, published by Argus Press Software, which was released in 1983.  The reconnaissance probe sent to the distant planet Astral 4 is on its way to return to Earth and provide all the information gathered during its search. But to refuel it will have to stop on one of the various planets it encounters from time to time. Retrieve the barrel of petrol using skillful use of the engines to oppose the different forces of gravitation and then enter the black hole to continue the journey. Be careful, because as you go through your journey the difficulties will increase and you will need your skills and alertness more and more. Released as part of "30 Games" game pack.

172391.overview: According to ancient Iridani law, the first born son of the Great Galactic Emperor has to participate in a Test of Arms to become Prince of the Southern Nebular and become first in line to the throne. You are Prince Kronos and your father is Iridon I and the time has come for you to take the test which means being transported to the toughest battlefield in the Universe, Earth. You have to visit five time zones and fight an opponent from each era in a one-on-one fight with a weapon to pass the test. The time zones are Caveman, Knights, Arabian, Pirates and a final battle in space. Each fight is seen from the side with each zone shown on the whole of the screen. There are two styles of game, a beat-em-up or a shooter. The Caveman, Knights and Pirates zones are all beat-em-ups and sees your hero with a weapon from that era. You have one attack but you can defend your opponents attacks as well. The Arabian and Space are shooters with each fighter facing each other on a magic carpet or wearing a jet-pack. Fireballs or lasers are fired at each other and when an opponent is beaten in a zone then you move to the next one until all are defeated. As the fights progress, there are three gauges to keep an eye on, Energy, Health and Weapon. The Energy gauge decreases every time you move or use your weapon. When you stop moving or using your weapon then it slowly increases. The Health gauge decreases every time you are hit by your opponent but items appear on screen which can be collected to increase it and you can also collect items to increase your energy. When either gauge have reached zero then you lose the fight but you get two more attempts to defeat your opponent. The weapon gauge will decrease when you use your weapon. When this reaches zero then you lose your weapon and leave you defenceless but one will appear and can be collected. Before you play the game there are various options that can be selected. Once fights have been won then that zone can be selected, you can choose your difficulty level (1-3), and either a one, two player game or a demo. Two player game sees you fighting in each zone and once a victor has emerged then both players fight in the next zone.

172393.overview: Based on the Star Wars films, this shoot-em-up is a Star Wars related game you may be unaware of, however feels like more work was put into the music than the game itself. It was developed by Cosine Systems (The late Jason Kelk did the code and graphics, and Gareth Dolloway did the SFX and music) Published in Commodore Zone Issue #11.

172394.overview: Personality Software That Lets You See People As They Really Are. Analyze anyone in your life. Get to know their secret likes and dislikes. Find out hidden truths about people you thought you knew Learn how to make the most of relationships and how to prevent emotional letdowns A self-help book\program on how to read others. Remember, it's not who you know, it's how well you know them.

172396.overview:
The Air Force has developed, in collaboration with a famous aeronaval construction company, a new aircraft that must be able, in the event of an attack by alien beings, to fight for the people of earth. But such a powerful and potent vehicle will be ineffective if good pilots capable of handling it are not trained. Since the conditions in which the aircraft will have to operate are for the moment still futuristic, the Air Force has built fantastic means to simulate the extraterrestrial attack and allow pilots to prepare. You too have had the opportunity to enter among these privileged ones and you have to demonstrate your skills in eliminating as many enemies as possible. 

Published in Italy as Fly in New Special PlayGames n.3 (novembre 1987) and in Hit Parade C64 n.22 (Aprile 1988).

172397.overview: This real time all-text game puts you in the role of a Mind Adventurer, asked to journey back through the minds of four deceased residents of your planet in search of the Wheel of Wisdom. The Wheel is the only thing that can restore your planet from the state of chaos it's now in. The hardbound book that comes with the game includes the instructions and a novella-length introduction to the plot.

172398.overview: An unpublished Pac-Man styled collect-em-up game for 1 player from MSC in 1990. It would later be heavily reworked and updated and released as Techno Plyn.

172399.overview: Mine Sweeper 9000 is a clone of classic Minesweeper. It allows to select difficulty level, customize board size, define controls, choose a background tune and save/load state of the game. All the other rules remain unchanged, including marking cells and mistake consequences.

172401.overview: Minefield is a clone of classic Minesweeper. The gameplay rules remain unchanged. Selected spot shows the number of bombs in the neighborhood. There is no possibility to select any gameplay aspects. The player has limited time to finish the board - 1000 seconds.

172402.overview: An implementation of Minesweeper for the C64 created by Christoph Cemper with music and SFX by Patrick Peters and published as part of Game On 1993/04.

172403.overview: Miner is a Boulder Dash clone developed by Øystein Berg and published by Data-Tronic. The year of release is not known. Unlike most Boulder Dash clones on the Commodore 64, this one was built from the ground up, and not made using the Boulder Dash Construction Kit. Berg programmed the game using just green, black, and some white to make it look as if it was done on a monochrome computer such as the Commodore PET.

172405.overview: The Master had given the order for all dragons to be killed. After the slaughter, it became apparent that one dragon, Cavilan, was missed. At the time of the slaughter she was in a cave giving birth to an egg. The Master, not happy with this, sent a band of orcs to finish the job off but Cavilan was missed again. The egg was found and taken away and stored in the Mines of Lithiad, hoping Cavilan would have come to rescue her unborn. Being too big to enter the mine she has asked yourself to rescue the egg and keep the dragons' heritage alive. The game is a text-adventure with no graphics. The screen describes your surroundings where you can enter commands to help you on your quest.

172406.overview: A game based on the Minesweeper game, but with increased difficulty based on the level.

172407.overview: A minesweeper puzzle game created by Dillo in 1992 and released by T'Pau Production.

172410.overview: A PETSCII racing game, a day at the speedway.

172412.overview: A 2D RPG game intended to be a mini-version of Ultima and part of the 2001 Minigame Competition 2K Category.

172413.overview: A single-screen pac-man game, possibly intended as a loader-game as the maze never changes and only 2 to 3 ghosts.

172414.overview: A boulder-dash style puzzle, action game published in 64'er Sonderheft 49.

172415.overview:
A stripped down, mini version of Tron, published in Magic Disk 64 1995/05. 

This fast-paced racing game is based on the movie Tron and is set in the distant future. Since the game was developed exclusively for two players, two joysticks must also be connected. With "+" and "-" you can regulate the speed and adapt it to your personal abilities. Only when both players press the joystick button does the game begin.

Each player controls a vehicle that leaves a trace on the race track. You must now be extremely careful not to touch your own trail or that of the opponent. That would mean one point for the opponent. Both players have the option of doubling the speed by holding down the fire button.
If a player has reached nine points, the game starts over. Have fun!

172416.overview: Mini-Zork has been compared to a Reader's Digest edition of a classic. The Mini-Zork is one of several remakings of Zork from the final years of Infocom. Mini-Zork I had a brief shelf-life in computer shops, in Activision packaging, but it is now best known for its magazine release. In November 1990, a year after Infocom had effectively become defunct, the Mini-Zork was given away with the British Commodore users' magazine "Zzap! 64" no. 67, which is now a collector's item.

172437.overview: Don your jetpack and we'll shoot our way into the heavily defended fortress. Avoid the guns and make your way past the traps and laser guardians to the heart of the citadel and take out the generators. It is a bit of a maze in there. Take out every brick in the protective walls and they will fall. We can be victorious.

172438.overview: Ebenezer Scrooge must perform a good deed to make up for his horrid existence, in fact he needs to perform 12 of them. Relive the struggles of Scrooge as he sets about his task. A task, which in his own eyes, was almost impossible. After all, it is bad enough that he should have to perform such deeds, but in order to do so he must first discover what the deeds actually are and how to perform them. Question everyone you pass, be observant and once you've finished your Herculean task, return to your nephew's house in order to finish the game.

172439.overview: The official game of the MISL, this game allows you to create an expansion team and build it into a championship franchise. You can trade and create players, modify team rosters, and train players for the season. Team stats are kept for 9 seasons, and the game offers the ability to coach, GM, play or all 3.

172441.overview: Miss Mind Ania is a puzzle-board game. The player's task is to guess the sequence of five digits in six attempts. At the top of the screen the player indicates digits from 0 to 9. The results of the trials are shown on the top right side of the screen: full dot (C64 - hearts) is a perfect match, half full dot (C64 - question mark) means that the digit occurs in a different place.

172442.overview: A missile command clone by Marc Gallo

172443.overview:
H_re'_ a _uzzle t_hat c_alleng_s yo_ _o re_d wo_ds a_d l_tte_s th_t ar_ n_t t_ere! Think you can do it? Good luck. o play, you reconstruct the passage by Filling in the missing letters, one-by-one. You win by filling in the most blanks with the fewest misses. Your guesses are based upon your built-in sense of language, your feeling for how letters make up words and words make up sentences. As the pas- Sage unfolds, you gain more clues for your next guesses.

The computer lets you vary the level of difficulty for each passage from omitting some of the letters to omitting all of the letters. Try it. You'll be
surprised how much you know. You can select passages from some of the classics of children’s literature including My Side of the Mountain; The Wind in the Willows; From The Mixed-Up Files of Mrs. Basil E. Frankweiler. The Lion, The Witch and The Wardrobe; The Cricket in Times Square; Shadow of a Bull; The Secret Garden, Little House in the Big Woods; and Charlie and the Chocolate Factory.

172448.overview:
A whimsical, ova themed collect'em up game published in Magic Disk 64 1988/06. 

It's the year 2020. After a nuclear war, the earth was devastated. But the surviving people have already adjusted to their new way of life. Actually, life goes on just as it did 33 years ago, but there are exceptions.

There are z. B. Giant chickens, which of course also lay giant eggs. The giant chickens just don't want to hatch their own eggs themselves. As a chicken farmer, you only have one option:

You have to take matters into your own hands. Fortunately, in this warm climate, which prevails all over the world, a small step (FIRE BUTTON) is enough for you to go against the giant eggs to bring the chicks to hatch.

However, these actions are not entirely safe, especially since there are radiation-contaminated clouds everywhere, which our chicken farmer PIT has to cleverly avoid. Any contact with the shadow of the clouds and the clouds themselves means death for PIT. Only the cloud that PIT constantly chases is harmless. Because this cloud is enriched with cosmic rays and only leads to a small change of location.
Fortunately, PIT can jump too. After pressing the SPACE key, PIT can break free from any predicament with one jump. But there the jumps at them
are limited to each level, you should divide the jumps well. 

The aim of the game is to free all chicks from their eggs and then to kick them off the screen with one last kick. If the chick and cloud collide while being ejected, the radioactive force of the cloud is discharged and the chick explodes. Since this effect also earns points and can also destroy dicey clouds that have come close, you should make use of this effect. In all the pictures there are small coins that can be picked up when PIT approaches them horizontally. These coins give bonus points when you reach a new level. Have fun!

172449.overview:
A Missile-Command clone game created by Jüggisoft and published in Magic Disk 64 1990/11. 

In this variation as well as defending against incoming ICBMs you need to defend the planet from the Romulan Warbirds and other alien ships. As fascinating as the game is, its instructions are simple. There are no cumbersome controls and no superfluous displays, and there is no great storyline either. Since CP-Verlag does not concern me with doing nothing, I will tell you a little bit more about MISSILE-COMMAND.

In the distant future: The extraterrestrials (who else?! In this regard It seems that from the year 2000 a lot is coming towards us earth dwellers...!) one is planning more of an attack on our good old earth. This time our friends have come up with something very special: We are being irradiated! Contrary to their usual practice, this time we don't have to shoot our way through countless waves of attack and bomber formations and - instead, stop the rays that are inexorably moving towards our mother planet with a gigantic rocket launcher.

In any case, it is important to prevent a jet from falling directly on one of the six cities and dissolving them into dust and rubble. It is therefore a matter of firing a rocket into orbit the descending rays. If the rocket explodes a little in front of the beam, the resulting short-term protective screen absorbs the attacker and thus renders him harmless. When all cities are hit and destroyed, the battle is lost!

Every now and then ships of the aliens cross the screen at great heights. If your hands are full, you might want to remember them and send them a missile or two. This not only has a positive effect on your points account, but also testifies to the great, unselfish commitment of your fellow players!

172451.overview: The security of the universe is in danger! Some evils placed several bombs in different systems. It's your task is to collect all the bombs and to make them inactive. You have only limited time until the bombs will explode!  Another one with shifty gravity. Watch those walls... too late... BOOM! Published in 64'er 1990/11, 64'er Sonderheft 73, 64'er 1998/08, SYS PD Diskett#49 (1994).

172452.overview: Pure arcade action! Ten levels featuring incredible life forms as you descent into the very depths of Jupiter!  Two player action with fantastic smooth scrolling graphics - a real challenge. You must conserve your fuel and laser power and whenever possible retrieve fuel and laser boosters from the planet surface.  The different life forms on each level have varying behaviour characteristics which  must be mastered in order to defeat them!

172472.overview:
A horizontally scrolling shooter.  Jump mines and obstacles in your armed jeep. Take out the baddies, bouncing balls, tanks and other foes. Set in the Vietnam war, Mission Monday\Tan is a game that takes place right in the middle of the conflict. The protagonist is a brave Sergeant Tan who has the important mission of delivering an urgent and very secret order to an outpost located in the middle of the jungle where there is a group of isolated soldiers. The enemy forces have surrounded the area and therefore our hero will need to do authentic stunts to complete the mission. Jump the mines that have been arrayed against you, destroy tanks, dodge traps and fight the soldiers and you will be able to complete Mission Monday. 

Published in Italy under the name Tan in various publications including Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - big 100 (1987), Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - maxi commodore (1988),  Special Games n.14 (giugno 1988) and Super C64 e C128 n.23 (maggio 1988).

172474.overview:
Published in Magic Disk 64 1992/04. 

We regret . . .  were the last words transmitted by the scouts who passed through the B-screens in the course of "MISSION NADA". So we are unable to tell you anything more that will prepare you for this mission. Since you have already shown courage in the face of death, by entering the kiosk and depositing 9.80 DM from the depths of your pants pockets and fearlessly placed the monies on the dark sales counter you are also free to enjoy the fulfillment of this task. So step in, and with your space glider on a journey into the unknown, fare well. We will not hold you back, but wish that if the Devil chases you, you will be faster than his trident.

172479.overview: A text adventure game written using AdventureWriter/Quill. Was also released as part of the "5 Adventures" game pack., sold at computer fairs and distributed through mailing lists, making them amongst the rarest of all C64 releases. You are taken by aliens to a distant planet simulated to look like an English village and your mission is to return to Earth.

172482.overview:
Psytronik Software in association with Magic Cap present an exciting new release for the C64 - MAZE OF THE MUMMY!  Featuring 15 Pyramids to explore (255 playable levels in total!) there's plenty of adventuring fun to be in your quest for treasure!
  
Use your wits and cunning to outwit the dreaded MUMMY lurking in his maze as you attempt to find 15 pieces of treasure.  Avoid the deadly SCORPIONS that patrol the rooms and search for keys that unlock more sections of the Pyramid.  Untold treasures await you if you are brave enough to enter - THE MAZE OF THE MUMMY!

172530.overview: A platforming game published in 64'er Sonderheft 37.
