The starbank of Astra, the richest deposit of precious gems and metals in the entire galaxy has always been considered an impregnable fortress, thanks to the highly sophisticated electronic alarm systems that control a myriad of unstoppable cyber guards. But for those charged with Mission X-2, the enterprise of robbing the big bank represents a goal and a challenge of great prestige. For this reason he has decided to challenge the impenetrability of the complex. While getting into it was a fairly easy feat, our hero will now have to contend with the infamous robotic hordes. The myriads of traps capable of incinerating anything face the your team. If you are skilled, you will be able to interfere in the control of the guardians from the numerous terminals or receive useful information to open the way to wealth and fame.

172531.overview:
An Italian language vertically-scrolling shooter based on Moon Cresta published in Linguaggio Macchina C64/ZX n.10 (Ottobre 1985).  
 
You can never be calm! Here, immediately after the signing of the intergalactic peace treaty, the rebels, who we believed by now subject, organized themselves to regain the upper hand over the galaxy. You had already parked your spaceship in the hangar, the agency had found you a holiday home on Mars and you thought you could finally enjoy a period of well-deserved rest but, now, you find yourself forced to take off to this new mission. It seems that at the Base they do it on purpose: as soon as you organize your holidays, they call you immediately for a new task! But by now you know that this is your destiny and you cannot change it. So put aside your thoughts and assumptions and... go. Your powerful and sophisticated spaceship is made up of three ships that you can only use once.

If you manage to pass the fourth game screen with the first and second, the three spaceships will "assemble" and you will be able to fight with a supercharged spaceship of the highest level and almost indestructible. Shoot the enemies with extreme precision, remember that if you don't hit their spaceships perfectly in the center, they will continue to fight and bomb you even if half disintegrated. A good game strategy may be to position yourself sideways on the screen at the start of the first massive attack by the enemy fleets to avoid being surrounded by the attackers. After this first attack you will be able to return to a central defense position. Watch out for phantom enemies that "take shape" when they're too close to you to dodge! Good luck... Mission H!

172532.overview: Create your model cars, give them Engines, transmissions and fuel systems and then take them out on the track for speed and handling trials.

172533.overview: This was a Japanese MAX cartridge release. These could be played on the C64 and were occasionally repackaged with a "slap-on" sticker and sold in Europe. Mole Attack is one of the earliest computerized Whac-a-Mole variants. Gameplay should be clear: Moles randomly pop out of several holes (arranged in a 3x3 grid), and you can hit them using the right keyboard key (one for each hole). The sooner you hit the mole's head, the more points you get -- but if you hit the mole's buttocks (yes, them buggers sometimes pop up that way), you lose points. After 60 seconds, the game ends and your score is shown.

172576.overview: With a shout-out to the Toronto PET User Group on the title screen, one of the longest continually operating Commodore centered user groups in the world it is hard to not consider this Collect-em-up style game as being associated with them. The fact that this is presented in all PETSCII means that this might have been ported to or from other Commodore systems. Maneuver your car through a deadly minefield, avoiding all the obstacles and collect money bags. Good luck!

172578.overview: Monkey Business is a puzzle game featuring a variant of the 'Towers of Hanoi' tile game. The player needs to help a stack of monkeys retrieve two apples from a tree. They are only allowed to move one monkey at a time, and players may only arrange the monkeys such that a smaller monkey is on top of a larger monkey. There are three locations the monkeys may be moved to, and by moving the monkeys around to the different locations, players can re-stack them under an apple so they may pick it. When both apples have been picked, the level is complete. The score is based on the number of moves it takes to complete this task. There are three skill levels, each of which have a different number of monkeys that must be manipulated.

172583.overview:
Learning math can be as fun as a barrel of monkeys! Monkeymath is an educational math game for multiple systems.

The player controls a monkey who works on an assembly line. They must punch the correct number fro 0 - 9 as it rapidly scrolls past to answer mathematical questions shown below. Allows for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, and counting questions of multiple difficulties. The monkey has a limited shift to work, and tries to maximize his score. Half way through the shift the monkey eats a banana for his lunch break

172584.overview: A vertically scrolling Shoot-'Em-Up Construction Kit based game where you and your buddy take on jets, other tanks and fortified positions while avoiding or destroying tank traps that block the way and limit maneuverability. One or two can play and it supports simultaneous 2 player, which is a real blast. Published in ECP's "War Games Pak" compilation.

172585.overview:
A Space Invader/Gorf style shooter where you are at Carnival but one where every joke counts. The aliens have camouflaged themselves as smiling masks, but underneath they are grim death dealing machines. They must be shot down mercilessly and not allowed to have the last laugh. Beware, they come from all directions, even below. 

Published in Italy as Le Machere in Supplementi Sipe - i Magnifici 10 (Settembre 1984).

172586.overview: Sunday, sunday, SUNDAY! It's  ground pounding, heart-stopping, quarter mile mayhem, as "Big Daddy" Don Garlits and Dan "the Snake" Purough chase 3-time top fuel eliminator World Champion, Shirley "Cha-Cha" Muldowney down the quarter mile of death in their seven-thousand horsepower nitro-burning suicide machines as they shake hands with the Devil when they scream through the burning gates of Hell. This game will sell you the whole front-row seat but you'll only need the edge! Be there!

172610.overview:
This is a space shooter, so the aliens must be the monster tribe in question. Or perhaps society is the tribe of monsters we all belong to that makes us want to kill anything alien. Xenophobic morality tale or a weekend blast of fun, you decide.
 
Monster Tribe is a 1-player arcade game for the Commodore 64.

The player controls a small spaceship that can move in all directions, and fires vertically forwards. The player finds 3 large alien creatures that move about the screen. When an alien is shot, they begin to return fire towards the player. The player receives points for hitting an enemy, but they can not be destroyed. They player starts with 5 lives, and loses a life if hit.

172611.overview: The aim of the game: You must walk through the labyrinth to reach the other side. Cruelly, monsters want to hit you and the walls are radioactive. You may not touch them and live!

172612.overview: Monsters is a Pac-Man variant. The player must eat all the objects on the board while avoiding constantly moving hostile creatures. Contact with any of them takes some amount of energy. There is no special dot, allowing to defeat enemies, therefore the game is all about a quick maneuvering of the character in order outwit the opponent. The game features 40 levels. This game was published in Reset #06 Mix-i-Disk.

172613.overview: A text adventure based RPG where your imagination is your video card and your computer is the Dungeon Master.  It will roll you up a character, assign hit points, give you starting gold and allow you to spend it on armor and weapons, it will help you level up as you explore and fight monsters in their lair.

172614.overview: Monstrum is a classic platformer, where the player must defeat a deadly creature hiding in the maze. Reaching the monster level requires finding numerous items and using them in an appropriate place, facing hordes of deadly enemies, such as mummies, knights or bats, several types of traps, including ground and rotating spikes. Appropriate use of the jumping skills, accurate knife throwing and timed stick hitting is the key to the success of the mission.

172615.overview: Published in Game On 1991/06.  Really quite fun Cybernoid-esque shooter/puzzle game in which you have to find the right keys for the right doors.

172642.overview: In this Frogger variant you need to dodge the planets and meteors and just from rocket ship to rocket ship in order to safely make your way to the docking bays across the way. Each docking bay you enter is now full and your choices of bay are limited until you fill all four and then it starts over, but with everything slightly more challenging.

172643.overview:
The title screen says this game was originally being made for Bubble Bus, which seems like either a big stretch or that Bubble Bus probably made the right move passing on this SEUCK created shooter. This is a vertically scrolling shooter with only forward offensive shooting capabilities. It does have bosses and multiple types of foes, decent graphics for the platform and nice backgrounds.  

It was published in Italy in the Alga Soft 1988 n.13b compilation.

172646.overview: Manoeuvre your jumping moon buggy over the moon's surface attempting to reach the landing pad on the other side without running out of fuel or crashing into a star mine. The moon buggy needs to build up thrust be careful because once "lift-off" has occurred it has a lot of forward momentum. The star mines are everywhere in space and you have to manoeuvre between them to get to the landing pad.

172677.overview:
This was a Balloon Rescue style game put in a space setting and with a collect-'em-up layer added to the tense time/fuel limits. This was released as the B side game of "To Hell and Back". Released in Italy as Cave Search in  New Special PlayGames n.13 (ottobre 1988). 

The brave ship has been commissioned to descend into the diamond fields of a dangerous lunar volcano: the aim of the mission is to collect as many of the Moon Crystals as possible before the volcano erupts. To do this the ship has a set of thrusters that will allow it to move quickly between the caves. Using it, however, requires some practice if you want to avoid crashing into the walls of the cave. Consumption of fuel must be watched, but you can restock by grabbing the fuel cans that have been seeded throughout the cave tunnels. Only after collecting all the gems from a section of caves will you be able to access the next set. There are 16 levels in all to complete the cave search.

172679.overview: Head to head simultaneous, fantasy-themed racing presented in a split screen view. Published in Italy in Formula 64 n.98 under the name Moon Racer.

172680.overview:
A single-player shooter, created by Cosmos Designs and published in both 64'er 1992/09 and 64'er 1997/12. So get your joysticks ready and off you go into battle against the enemy fighters. Their elite units are called to arms by the Central Council of Humanity and the denizens of the worlds hope for a victory against the behemoths. The task is to eliminate the hordes and to destroy their space cruisers, on which new combat machines are constantly being developed and built... 
 
Ever since the fateful experiment on the planet Gerkatas, humanity has been on alert. A dozen worlds have already had to abandon their inhabitants to the biomechanical monsters bred on Garkatas. These creatures are extremely intelligent and very aggressive. Actually, one wanted to colonize worlds with the beings that were uninhabitable for humans and to cultivate them with the help of bio-creations. But after the generator for the charisma insert complex failed, the experiment went awry and the new beings evolved into predatory, murderous monsters.
Now the beings want to wipe out humanity and take possession of the universe. So they have built space fleets with gigantic ships and are heading for the central solar system. At intervals, they send their space fighter commands to terminate the human battle fleet

172681.overview:
This game was the prototype version of Idea Software's MoonShadow, which was a prequel to Zone Trooper, but many, many changes were made to it and the music and graphics in the latter game were different in multiple ways. Where Zone trooper would mostly be described as shooter, this game was more of a multi-screen platformer. Add to that the fact that this had one of the best title screens in the late 80's and it is a fun addition to your collection, especially if you enjoy Zone Trooper.
 
Published in Italy's Videoteca Computer n.3 as Jet Trooper and as Astroenergy in Nova Games n.19 (Aprile 1988).

172682.overview:
A game by Thomas  and published in Computronic 1985/11-12. A 3D game with all the trimmings! You find yourself on a dangerous space patrol. The background moves really three-dimensionally. The game takes you to the moon Lima, better known as "Moon" you will fly patrol with your super modern space glider.  
 
On your way across the surface of the moon you will encounter strong fleets of "aliens" who will give you quite a bit of trouble. They say: "Escape or shoot down the enemy spaceships!" Another kind of "source of danger" are the laser towers, which suddenly emit deadly lasers - either to the left or to the right (you have to wait and then dodge). There are also true kamikaze UFOs and mother ships emerging from space, the Make them really hard, so fire from all guns to escape this hell relatively unscathed! You go through several rounds during the (successful) game. The change of rounds is made clear by the different color of the lunar surface. You have to survive five rounds in total, with rounds 4 and 5 featuring significantly faster attackers. Of course, there are points for every goal, and after the game you can "immortalize" your glorious name in the Hi-Score table. 

But note: you lose energy every time you collide with the enemy or if you come into contact with the lasers. This decreases accordingly until you have breathed your "moon life" last breath. Released in the UK as part of the Golden Oldies compilation.

172683.overview:
You are the janitor in the worst school possible. You must clean the whole school in sections while being attacked by pupils, teachers and even dogs. To top it all off you've got a bad back which gets worse the more you clean. When your back finally goes then you'll have to spend a week to recover. Never fear though, you have weapons at her disposal like soap which can be thrown or a smart-bomb type substance called Gleamo - which kills and cleans everything in sight. The more you clean the more moola you make. 

The game is viewed from above and is a multi-directional game. You control mopper and each section must be cleaned and a certain amount of enemies have to be killed to progress. All this has to be done within a time limit which is based on your bad back. The more that is cleaned, the more money you earn. You also need to keep your bucket full as well and if nearly empty you have to find places to fill it back up.

172687.overview: Moonraid is a simple horizontal scrolling shooter developed by Mark Kiddell and published by Binary Zone PD in 1992.

172693.overview:
This game is interesting in a way, but suffers from much wordiness, which
appears to be irrelevant (at least to Part 1). You are never really clear
on the objective. Hints are given in poetry form. You often need to cast
spells which you can do if you have the page placed in the book. Hence the
first priority is to find in book into which you can put the spells. Some
of the hints are very obscure, or are typographical errors, for example,
the word "spell" appears to mean to rearrange letters, though "nopw", which
seems to means "open" may be a mistake.



There seem to be at least 13 pages, only which a few can be located in part
1, some of which are usable in this part, others not; some of which may
refer to the same thing but in a different way. Others do not appear to be
available in this part. TAKE PAGE will put it in the book; PAGE # allows
you to read the page.

The game comes in four parts/acts

172701.overview: An early Edutainment game aimed at teaching advanced strategic thinking and reasoning. The game is comprised of 7 sub-games that also introduce pattern recognition and problem solving, all involving the Moppets of Moptown.

172702.overview: One of the oldest releases by The Learning Company, Moptown Parade is an edutainment game aimed at teaching basic pattern recognition and logic skills to kids aged 4-7. The goal is simple: choose the traits of Moppet creatures to line up in a queue, obeying the given number of rules. For instance, if the rule says "2," you must choose the traits of the next Moppet so that it differs from the previous Moppet by 2 traits, e.g. a fat, blue Moppet can stand next to a thin, red Moppet. The number of rules, i.e. traits, can be changed from 1 to 4, thus either making the game more or less challenging (although changing the traits to 4, the maximum, will just result in your Moppets being an alternate sequence of two types of Moppets).

172703.overview: A single-screen at a time platformer created by Twice Effect where you must gather the diamonds and treasure to be transported to the next and more difficult level. You have the ability to create stepping stones to move around the screen, but you can make only a limited amount and must complete the level as the clock ticks down. Published in Game On 1993/06.

172704.overview:
Morph is the C64 conversion of the 1993 Amiga game, Pollymorph,  a single-player colour-matching puzzle game.

In this game the player controls a small ball that can be used move other balls around. When two same-coloured balls meet they disappear and the game objective is to clear the game area by pushing balls of the same colour together.

The number of balls and the complexity of the game area increases as the player progresses through the game.

172718.overview: An aerial duel game for 2 players. Pick your planes and go head to head. 3 planes to choose from and shoot it out.

172752.overview: Published in both Happy Computer 1987/07 and 64'er Spielesammlung #4, this Tron Light Cycles game is for 2 player only head-to-head play.

172754.overview:
Published in RUN 1988/11 (Issue #59) and in Radio Elettronica & Computer 1989/11. Racing a motocross motorcycle requires courage, skill and 
quick reactions. While courage is not necessary for playing C-64 Motocross, the skill and Quick reactions are. By pressing the C (lefl) and M (right) keys, you are scored on your ability to guide a motorcycle between markers on a narrow, unpredictable, computer-generated race course. 

Motocrossers. start your computers!

172755.overview: A game of the "Cassette 50" collection. Cross the road and rescue the girl. Move along from let to right but look out for the cars! Possibly the very worst attempted Frogger style game anyone ever paid money for, so it is the best at being the worst. It has that going for it.

172769.overview: A 2 player only puzzle game published in 64'er 1991/11. As a mental challenge, we can recommend the game by Daniel Schulz. The game is played in pairs using a joystick. The game is a grid of seven times seven squares, on which each player has 24 stones in an even distribution. Logically, one field remains empty. It is now alternately moved into the respective empty field, either one's own or an opponent's piece can be moved. Only a stone that has just been moved must remain standing on the next move. Whoever manages to get four of their own stones connected in a row or column or, if you are very tame, to have them brought. A new game starts with a touch of the SPACE key. If this seems too easy for you, after loading the game you can use POKE 325X,(number-l)  there the number of connected stones required can be increased if you think your nerves can take the strain.

172770.overview: A puzzle game from Ingo Kusch and published in Game On 1993/06. The universe's entropy level collapsed and the only chance to rescue the universe is an attempt to stop the increasing entropy chaos by "recombinating" the disordered structures. The icons on your screen belong to separated and disordered energy structures which have to be recombined my moving them. Match icons together where they will annihilate themselves. And this is how you will decrease entropy. Also watch out for bombs and transmitters which have special effects on their surroundings.

172771.overview:
A puzzle\brain\logic game published by Magic Disk 64 1991/01. 

Push the boxes down the grates and listen to some pretty good music while you do it! Never before have we presented you a game on MAGIC DISK that corresponded more to reality than this, called MOVE OUT! Take on the responsible work of an employee of the CP-Verlag field service department and do your best - you will see that this is a lot of fun, but also requires a little imagination and ingenuity and also has a huge advantage: You save yourself to hire us as a temporary worker during the next vacation (be honest: That was always one of your greatest dreams, wasn't it? But don't worry - many thousands of other MAGIC DISK readers feel the same way!) and you can use the days off enjoy somewhere on a cozy, warm sandy beach in the distance! You have still not really worked for us, but MOVE OUT has meanwhile conjured up an (almost) original atmosphere of work in our home, and so you will have yourself at the latest after the 3rd Level swore never to touch a broom less than 15 DM an hour again! That's right - have a nice vacation!

That nobody gets me wrong now: What is called for is not working in the editorial office (i.e. writing texts, making phone calls, eating pizza, etc.), but the extremely tough job in the warehouse! Yes, the current issue of MAGIC DISK has been created, copied and packaged ready for dispatch and now only has to be delivered. Your task now is to use a fork lift truck to move the wooden boxes with the magically valuable freight that are lying around wildly around the nested hall (old buildings are simply cheaper to rent!) Into the freight elevator, one after the other. Unfortunately, the boxes are much too heavy to be our high-. . . Excuse me, the forklift could lift it and the only option left is to push it towards the exit. But be careful: one wrong push, the box is in the corner or on a wall, can no longer be moved (because it cannot be pulled out), and one shift (= one life) is forfeited!
There are easier and harder setups, because our warehouse workers leave everything standing and lying with the gong at the end of the day, and depending on the situation, the situation is sometimes more and sometimes less complicated for you. "It is the man himself" is our motto, and so on you also have to judge for yourself whether the current line-up can still be achieved. If not, just press SPACE , your life will be deducted and everything will start all over again. Each loaded edition of MAGIC DISKS earns 10 points on the account! 
 
Of course, you can also bribe the warehouse workers with a case of beer. These then move away with them beaming with joy, but not without having adjusted the numerous boxes as desired beforehand (in good German: MOVE OUT also has an editor built in with which you can develop your own set-ups according to your wishes!).

172772.overview:
A puzzle game that is quite a challenge, created by Danial Schaack and published in Game On 1994/04.

In this game you can slide pieces around to create matches that are removed from the playing area, allowing you to slide and match more until the level is clear, and you can move on to the next head-scratcher.

172774.overview: Learn to make your own movie for the C64.

172777.overview: A Catch-it game like Kaboom, created by Jörg Fischer and published in the German magazine, 64'er 1991/08.

172781.overview: Helps children develop computer programming skills as they have fun creating designs and drawings.

172782.overview: Contains "Animal Wildcard" & "Switcharoo" matching games similar to the memory board game.

172783.overview: Mr. TNT is an arcade game where the player controls the titular blobby character. The game is played on a grid and the player's objective is to collect sixteen stockpiles of dynamite. Lit fuses are also moving across the grid and the player has to avoid touching these or he will explode. The grid is removed as the player or the fuses move across it which means the player can't turn around and move in the opposite direction. It also means that he has to plan his movements to avoid reaching a dead end. The same is true for the fuses who will burn out when reaching a dead end. A level is cleared when the player has collected all the dynamite or when all fuses have been burned out. The player then moves on to another level with a different grid layout. Points are earned by picking up dynamite and for crossing grid junctions.

172797.overview: A 2P Only (Simultaneous) game with top and bottom split screen for head to head action. A favorite of C64 convention tournaments. Released in Valueware - Educator II.

172798.overview:
Published in 64'er 1994/07, this is a game version of Mühle, also known as Nine Men's Morris or Merels.  Nine Men's Morris, also known as Merrills, Mill and Merels, is an old English game that goes back to antiquity - evidence has been found for the game in ancient Rome and possibly Ancient Egypt. More recently, references in the works of Shakespeare have given it an image of the archetypal medieval board game.

Like most of the best games, Nine Mens Morris rules are simple, the objective being to capture opposing pieces by forming lines of 3. It is an under-rated game of skill that is easy to learn but sometimes requiring deep thought - a bit like grown-up tic-tac-toe (or noughts and crosses). It is an entertaining game for beginners and veterans alike and something for older children and adults to enjoy.

172799.overview: A two-player, simultaneous Pac-Man game published in Game On 1992/11. You can play single player as well.

172803.overview: A simple Pac Man style game that was part of the "Arcade Games (3 Pack)", the Australian Galaxions/Munchman combo pack and "Arcade Games I" pack. Munch your way around the maze, eating the dots, while avoiding the 4 hungry ghosts. A power pill in each corner of the maze, when eaten, allows you to gobble the ghosts for a short time. Delicious fruits yield high bonus points and a free muncher is given at 20,000 points. The cart version features a two player option.

172804.overview:
COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1983/11 (Issue #5), COMPUTE!'s Second Book of Commodore 64. The Compute!'s Gazette issue also features a version for the VIC-20 as well.

It was later released as party of The Big 100 compilation in Europe under the name Muchman.

172806.overview: Published in both Commodore Disk User 1990/06, and in Your Commodore 1990/09 (Tape #08). This is a Pac-Man clone, and definitely not worried about copyright issues.

172813.overview: Muppets on Stage contains three different stages for children to choose from: Discovery for keyboard exploration, Letters for upper and lower case letter identification and Numbers where children must correctly identify the number of pictures shown on the screen with several levels of difficulty. Intended for children from Kindergarten to First Grade, but may be effectively used in special Education settings.

172818.overview: A murder has occurred at the castle of Lord and Lady Osbourne, and you have been called in to solve this murder mystery. After the crime occurred, the murderer ran from the room and threw the murder weapon into another room. At that time, the corpse was discovered and it was decided that everyone would remain where they were until you can arrive, question them, examine the evidence and solve the mystery.

172819.overview: A strategy game where you are the detective and must interrogate suspects, gather information and accuse the one who the must be the murderer.

172820.overview: A talking graphic text adventure. You are the ill-fated adventurer and must find Mary before her time is up and she ends up dead.

172821.overview: A text adventure written with AdventureWriter\Quill and part of "The Lockerby Collection". Find and kill a dangerous mutant creature roaming the area.

172822.overview: A logic puzzle game created by Michael Trede and published in 64'er Sonderheft 79.

172823.overview: Only a hero of the greatest magnitude could fix the printer. Are you that hero?

172824.overview: You've read the game, now play the book! Based on the best-selling Puffin book by John Astrop. This is a game, but it is also a personal database for your darkest thoughts. Do you have secrets you wouldn't even confide to your closest friend, let alone your family? Do you have secrets about your friends and family you wouldn't confide to anyone but yourself? At last, you're no longer alone. My Secret File turns your computer into a personal confidante. And to keep your confidences confidential, it's even password protected, because these days, you can't even trust your micro not to blab. Trust no one: file your friends before they file you.

172841.overview: A screen by screen platformer that was released as part of "Arcadepack" by Multisoft.

172842.overview:
A very UnPacman-like Pac-Man clone published in Magic Disk 64 1989/01.

The aim of the game is to collect all the points on the screen in order to reach the next level. However, four monsters try to thwart this. Fortunately, there are power pills that Mysterix can take, whereupon the monsters turn blue and Mysterix can eat them. The eaten monsters cannot harm the hero until they transform back into shape. A game editor is also included.

172844.overview: A scrolling Screen Platformer very much like Mario Bros/Giana Sisters made by Jan Zimmermann and Ulf Denzin and published in Magic Disk 64 1995/08. The player's task is to rescue two brothers kidnapped by an evil witch. During the journey, the player will find upgrades that allow them to destroy brick platforms or shoot. Unfortunately, losing a life also results in the loss of upgrades. The game also features hidden rooms with lots of coins that add a life if the player collects 100 of them.

172845.overview: A puzzle game created by Harald Sprung and published in 64'er 1997/05 / a.k.a. "Mystify".

172856.overview: Search Mystery Island for the treasures hidden there. You will have to have your wits about you to find all of them. Get all the treasures and deposit them into the cave behind the waterfall. You can carry 5 items so take 2 trips to store all 10 treasures.

172868.overview: You find yourself lying on a raft floating in the middle of the sea with no land or anything in sight after you had to abandon ship with the rest of the crew into shark infested waters. Your aim in this three part text adventure is to get yourself back home as you face various challenges and quests, as well as face many monsters and creatures on your travels. Each location is described by text and you type in with the keyboard, commands to control your hero and interact with the locations. Each time a character speaks to you, you can hear it with digitised speech.

172872.overview:
In this one, you are a H.E.R.O-lookalike who must get through 12 rooms to collect all the gems. You are armed with a grappling-hook that gets you from platform to platform, and occasionally a gun.

This game was developed by Jörg Dierks, and published by Data Media in Germany in 1985.

172929.overview:
A boxing game for 0 to 2 simultaneous players, released as Megabox in Go Games n.13 (October 1986). A boxing match where you fight against a champion guided by the computer or against a second participant. I want a good, clean fight so touch globes and go back to your corners and when the bell rings come out swinging. 

Published as Megabox in Italy in Go Games n.13 (Ottobre 1986).

172972.overview: The Slicker Puzzle is a puzzle game that is played on a 16 by 16 grid that show a pattern. Each square of the grid contains two triangles: one that is black and one that is of another colour. After choosing a skill level the grid is shuffled and the player's task is to recreate the original pattern of the grid. This is done by moving lines either vertically or horizontally. For each move made a line is moved one step down or to the right. If the puzzle is completed within the correct number of moves then a coded message will be displayed. By completing the eight skill level the message is decoded.

173427.overview:
A Q-bert style action puzzle game that was part of the French "3 Super Jeux" game pack. Inspired by the arcade game Q*Bert, you take the role of Pancho who has to paint all the squares on various heights in a isometric view on a single screen. To paint a square, all Pancho has to do is land on a square but needs to avoid a Mad Mexican Muncher that moves around the screen and if he touches it then he loses one of three lives. Also moving around the screen is a wild jumping bean that changes the squares back to their original colour but this can be caught to remove it.

Pancho starts a level on one of two magic carpets and these can be stood on to have a breather as the Muncher can't land on them. Pressing the fire button anywhere on the screen transports Pancho on to one but this can only be done four times. Once the level has been cleared then it's onto the next one but with more Munchers and the squares have to be landed on more than once to paint them.

173958.overview:
A superb remake of the Matthew Smith classic developed and coded by Graham "Toki" Axten (The Bear Essentials, Bonkey Kong, Dustin', etc.) and released December 29, 2019. Unlike the original C64 version, this version plays more like the original version that Matthew Smith developed himself on the ZX Spectrum. However, you have a choice to play either the original C64 version, or the 2019 remake in the game's startup screen. The game also has a built-in "trainer" in it's options menu.

Description:

You play the role of Miner Willy, a bold explorer and adventurer. He discovers a network of underground caverns used by an advanced but now extinct civilization, and realizes that the mines contain lucrative metal ores. Through 20 caverns, you must collect all treasures before all time (air) runs out, watching out for the nasty guardians, the obstacles, dead falls, quicksands and all elements to be found in a classic platform game.

174144.overview: A horizontally scrolling Moon Lander style shooter game.

174293.overview: A clone of Arkanoid: Revenge of Doh with some minor modifications, published in Italy in Super Game 2000 Nuova Serie N°05 (Aprile 1988).

174297.overview: A rather odd variation on Tetris. Pushing up or down selects one of four tiles that is falling, fire spins it, and left/right moves it. The game was published in Game On 1992/09.

174298.overview:
The  remixed version of Mega Starforce - Return to the Great Star. 

Obviously this a one of those thrillion space invaders clones but the makers really did a good job here. The graphics are brilliant, the music is awesome but most important of all, the gameplay is fantastic! this game simply rocks, play it! Hacker's version. This game will load levels into extended RAM if you have it.

174396.overview: Let your computer teach you professional magic, or at least some tricks that can be easily translated into simple graphics and presentation.

174737.overview:
A puzzle and logic game created by Daniel Horst and published in Magic Disk 64 1990/06 in Germany and in International Games n.3 (marzo 1991) in Italy under the name Murator.

Quadrato is a puzzle game where the aim is to place all the stones in the holes provided for them. While this sounds simple enough, it does take some thought.

175592.overview: An Arkanoid style Pong\Breakout game with money bricks that drop, you can use the money to buy special power ups that can help in clearing the level. Published in Italy in Special Program n.81 (novembre 1991), Computing videoteca Nuova serie - Mattoni Elettronici 2 and in Videoteca Computer n.31.

175749.overview:
A two pack of text adventure mysteries, written in Adventurewriter/Quill including  "The Mystery of the Clock Seller" & "The Adventure of the Rosetta Stone".

The Mystery of the Clock Seller: The game finds Holmes and Watson trying to unravel the events that led to the death of Otto Meinwold - seller of fine antique clocks. Scotland Yard thinks the case is rather clear-cut. That Meinwold, found strangled with a pendulum cord from a Grandfather clock, was murdered for the daily take from his shop. Holmes believes there is much more to it.

The Adventure of the Rosetta Stone: Holmes is up against the mysterious "French Reclamation League" and their threat to steal this famous artifact.

175758.overview: A brain\logic puzzle game published in Game On 1992/04 and in Italy in Tutto C64 n.2 (1992/1993.

175890.overview: This text adventure and its sequel, Dial M for Marlo were released in Loadstar magazines, this one published in both Loadstar #223 and Loadstar #246. Our favorite hard-boiled PI is back in a great text adventure and it is YOU! Sammy Marlo, distant cousin to Phillip Spade, returns to seek out clues and solve a mind-numbing mystery. That is, you do. You find the clues and put together the evidence. You make the collar, or you get in trouble with the cops.

175932.overview:
Mine Canyon is an avoid-it game for the Commodore 64. It was developed by John Krutch and published by Ion International, Inc. in Ahoy! 1986/09 (Issue #33).

The game is also known under the names Run Throught and Lauf Durch!

176283.overview:
THE WORLD NEEDS YOU!

The Apocalypser has been activated. Turn it off before it brings Earth to an end.

Protovision and RGCD are proud to present MAH, a frantic-paced, immersive, rich, and totally innovative cyberpunk arcade game developed by Retream. Your objective is to stop the Apocalypser's 90 minutes countdown with your Peekpoker tool by hacking through the ApocalypShield, a software system made of 24 security layers and defended by numerous virtual guards.

176323.overview:
An unofficial sequel to the well known Pinball game by the group Fairlight. In principle the same pinball only with improved graphics and covered SID tunes... also the physical behaviour seems to have changed.. 
 
Published in Italy by Pubblirome\Edigamma publishing as Mega Tilt in Super C64 e C128 n.34 (maggio 1989) and several other publications.

176531.overview: During a routine orbit of Saturn you encounter a radiation storm which forces you into the rings causing you to lose your ships energy. The only solution is to make an emergency landing on the planet's surface which was successful and luckily you landed next to an old abandoned mine full Di-Lithium Crystals. Your mission now is to enter the mine and collect enough crystals to re-fuel your ship and leave Saturn.

176841.overview: Monster Caves is a text adventure game developed by Todd Harrison and Les Battyanyi and published by Fontana Paperbacks as a type-in from the book "Giant Book of Games for You Commodore 64"

176902.overview: A snake-style action game. Players guide a snake around a field with varying obstacles; the goal is to eat all of the mushrooms to proceed to the next level. Each time the snake eats a mushroom, it gets longer; a life is lost if the snake crashes into walls or itself. Published in Keypunch software's Adventure Quest IV game collection, as a game of "The Big 100" collection / a.k.a. "Worms" and in Your Computer magazine 1984/07.

176942.overview: A Worm/Snake game with added collect-em-up fruit. Published in Paper Soft 1985/03 (25.01.1985), and in Commodore Club N°02 as "Cobra".

177126.overview:
Megamania 64 is a 2020 homewbrew conversion of the classic Activision Atari game Megamania. This version was developed by Arlasoft and published on his itch.io page. The game is available for free download.

Game description: 

MegaMania is an arcade action game with gameplay similar to Space Invaders. You control a spaceship at the bottom of the screen and need to defend yourself from numerous waves of attackers. But in MegaMania, the attackers are much more bizarre than invading aliens. There are hamburgers, diamonds, steam irons, bow ties, space dice, and more! You need to earn points by destroying as many of these strange attackers as you can before your energy supply becomes depleted.

177442.overview:
Psytronik Software presents MARS (aka MARTE), a game for the Commodore 64 by Sputnik World.  Released 50 years after man first set foot on moon now here's you chance to take a giant leap even further - on a mission to the red planet, MARS! The human adventure continues ...


** THE GAME **

 Humanity is on the verge of taking a great leap and starting one of the greatest adventures in history - A mission to MARS.
 
You are the mission commander and you have eight of the best international space engineers in your crew. It is up to you to keep the health of your crew as stable as possible during the mission. Issue commands to your crew members in order to complete your mission - each crew member is responsible for different tasks.  Keep an eye on your energy level and the status of your crew. There will be many problems that you will have to face and solve during your mission to reach the red planet.

177535.overview: In the game simulating some kind of golf you should complete the course consisting of 18 stages, putting the ball into the hole with as less strokes of the ball as possible. Each stage is presented on one screen in top-down view, it has a different shape, and different obstacles or gates are set to be avoided or passed through. Setting the ball in the field, you should select the direction and power of the stroke. The points at the end of each stage are calculated as subtraction of made strokes and pre-defined ones different for each stage. The winner is a golfer with a lowest number of points. The number of players (1-4), their names, and courses may be adjusted before the start. In multiplayer mode, each player strikes their balls in the separate fields in turns.

177616.overview: Moon Train is a Danish type-in shooter published in the Danish publication: SOFT Special #85/1 (Januar 1985) / no definite name, called "Månelokomotiv" in the magazine, it was written by Kurt Andersen. It sounds somewhat like science fiction, and it is. Would you like to be a locomotive driver on the moon, the day spies and DSB lay the first line across it's face? In this Commodore 64 game you get the opportunity to play locomotive drivers, and the work is at least as demanding and dangerous as in the good old Western days of raids and Indian attacks. On the Moon, it's just UFOs and mines that make you dizzy. However, you do have some defensive options. You can jump with the H key and shoot down enemies with SPACE.

177976.overview: An educational - vocabulary/language game for one or two players created by Vince Apps and released in 1984 in the book "40 Educational Games for the Commodore 64". If you are one of those poor souls who are always being told by someone that you miss letters in words don’t worry too much because it’s supposed to mean that you are clever and that your brain works faster than your hands. However, it’s not a good idea to go on doing it so we have invented this game to help you. Words are going to appear on the screen and you are going to have to spot the missing letter. If your answer is correct the computer will tell you that your decision was correct, award you a number of points depending on the speed of your response and move on to the next word. Wrong answers will mean no points and the computer will move on to the other player - if there are two playing.

178599.overview:
This is a compilation that contains the following 7 games (plus one free):

•  Arkanoid
•  Cobra
•  Frankie Goes to Hollywood
•  Head Over Heels
•  Short Circuit
•  The Great Escape
•  Wizball
•  Yie Ar Kung-Fu

179263.overview:
You are in the orbit of the moon of Geevor on your Comet Starfighter and your task is to protect its precious mines by finding and destroying as many Scavenger ships as possible during your watch. Although the Scavenger shuttles are difficult to locate, the infrared screen of your Comet will easily identify them, indicating your position in relation to them. You will have to approach the enemy at high speed, decreasing it you are in range to fire to increase accuracy. You have friends to help, remember that laser cannons are inactive against them. When comets approach you will need to dodge them to continue fighting.

Published in Italy as Comet Starfighter in Special PlayGames n.16 (marzo 1986).

179430.overview:
An early version of Hero of the Golden Talisman, which is quite a bit different, featuring different music, screens, enemies and a rather bizarre swimming animation! It was leaked to the scene and has been floating around under a number of different pseudonyms including "Labyrinth" and "Progfine" at one point.
 
Published in Italy as Minaccia al Mondo in Logica 2000 n.18 (Marzo 1986).

179527.overview: Published in Your Computer #7 / English translation added unofficially. Your goal is to destroy all possible aliens before they turn deadly. Hordes of descending aliens are hell-bent on destroying your ship. You will need very quick reactions and a fast trigger finger if you want to survive in this very fast machine code game. In addition to the normal options, you can choose the size of the aliens and whether or not there will be any wreckage around which to navigate.

179809.overview:
You are a brave adventurer, and your quest is to find and explore a Magic Castle to rescue a Princess trapped in the tallest tower. You must be wary of boobytraps and other creatures which are trying to kill you. Magic Castle is a text adventure where the screen has text describing each location that you visit and you type in commands with the keyboard to interact with your surroundings.

The game was written in The Quill Adventure Writing System - a utility to create adventure games developed by Gilsoft which was later extended by The Illustrator - an add-on pack that enabled users to add location graphics to their games. Besides providing the tools to create adventure, Gilsoft also released several of its own titles under the Gold Collection label. "Magic Castle" was one of them.

180079.overview:
A logical brain game published in Magic Disk 64 1995/08. Bruno is a warehouse worker at CP-Verlag. His working day is long and arduous, his wages and remuneration, like that of the editors, meager and small. Bruno's job is to bring the heavy pallets with the recorded Magic Disks to the freight elevator. However, since the data carriers are just stuffed full of cool games and programs, Bruno can only push them forward, but not pull or even lift. This is a real problem. 

You now have the unique opportunity to slip into the role of Bruno and to do his heavy day's work completely free of charge, on a voluntary basis and above all for nothing (and someone else said that we wouldn't offer our readers anything!). But be careful: first think, then press!
Bruno is controlled with a joystick in port 2. If you want to push a box, then you have to keep the fire button pressed and steer it in the appropriate direction. As it will happen sooner or later (at the latest in the second level) that you have played yourself into a dead end, then you can throw the symbolic towel in exasperation by pressing the space bar, deducting a life and then you may attack the level again from the beginning. 

In order to make the work in the stuffy disk warehouse really uncomfortable, Bruno also has to fight against a merciless time limit. The clock is running visible to the player and when it has expired before Bruno has heaved all the boxes into the elevator, the angry foreman rushes over immediately with the hippopotamus whip. Out of consideration for our younger players (and the federal testing agency for extremely violent games) we left this sequence and the subsequent punitive action hidden. Note anyway: dawdling is not!!  

 (= at Game Over) Bruno still has the opportunity to immortalize himself with the employees of the month. You can also hide the music in the main menu or return to an earlier save by entering a code word. To do this, simply steer Bruno around as usual and push a crate onto the desired option.
After this game, think twice about whether you really want to contact CP Verlag for holiday work in August...

180176.overview: A pinball game created in Pinball Construction Set and published in the PCS Club Disk #02, and in Stonysoft #1725

180262.overview: Published in Commodore Disk User 1988/07-08, as well as Your Commodore 1991/03 (Tape #15), and GO64! 2005/10. Explore the president's brain and find out what kind of guy is entrusted with the button to end all civilization. A summit conference of the world's two military giants is scheduled for tomorrow, but for no very good reason the US president has gone totally insane. Well, not totally insane, one coherent idea remains alive deep within his subconscious. It is your mission, should you accept it, to guide this small bubble of sanity through the labyrinth of the president's mind, destroying insane thoughts and opening the doors of reason. Ultimately you must find the exit from his subconscious and enter the president's conscious mind, restoring his sanity. The president's subconscious is made up of a 10 x 16 grid of 256 rooms. Each room is full of insane thoughts which must be blasted. When a certain number of thoughts have been destroyed (this number is different for each room) the doors will begin to open. The player can then pass through these into the next room, and when the exit is reached, sanity is restored.

180268.overview: An extended and fully playable preview game.

180277.overview: Judged harshly as #6 in the Mixed Competition at 2003 MiniGame Compo. Nice 4K Arkanoid game with powerups, music and all that it needs

180289.overview: A Moon Patrol clone that was intended to be a Moon Patrol Trainer, but it seems like it got out of hand and ended up being it's own creation. Published in Italy in Alga Soft n.17a.

180306.overview: Frogger inspired game called 'Mashed Turtles', which has been released for the C64. This game originally developed by Fandal+PG for the Atari 8bit, is a multiplayer port by Angelsoft, with spirtes by Dorndof that supports up to 8 players of turtle squashing fun. Requires a multiplayer hardware adapter for more than 2 players.

180329.overview: A vertically scrolling SEUCK based space shooter developed by Precision Designs and published by Disk User in 1989.

180331.overview: A rather tough, multiple choice Middle Earth Quiz published in Loadstar #002.

180332.overview: A Missile Command clone coded entirely in BASIC. Shoot your anti-missile weapon and save the cities from destruction. Published as a type-in game in the book "PCW Games Collection for the Commodore 64".

180333.overview: Officer, your mission is to deploy the research sensor that will us to look for water on the moon underground. This is essential for our plans to build the first lunar base. Keep a keen eye on your fuel, if you run out there won't be a rescue.

180350.overview:
But why is the name Mutilator used? Well, just to make things pretty funny in the game, you are able to mutilate cows during your travelling across planet Earth, as well as fighting the army forces. What a cruel thing 1 alien vs loads of armed forces :) 
 
The game was produced for Digital Talk #90 disk magazine.

180351.overview: A compilation package of Mysterious Adventure No.1 - No.6 - they are available separately too. This had a single loader on one disk and was released for Atari 800, C64 and the Dragon 32 and may have had some of the cheapest packaging that Channel 8 ever used, manual and disk in a bag apparently. Still, for text adventure fans, what a deal.

180352.overview:
A Junior edition, (für Kinder) of the 1984 Mr. Robot and his Robot Factory game. Dear little Dwarfs, 
Enjoy this fabulous game from 1984 without any pressure. jump and collect as much as you want! Avoid fire and deep falls. You can choose the Junior Edition or the original when you are ready. You can skip levels and pause the game. Warning: on nice days go play outside.

180355.overview: The revenge of Sasha the poo colored cat with a name ripped from an episode of The Simpsons.

180363.overview: A compilation of Mysterious Adventure No.7 - No.11 - they are available separately too.

180430.overview: Published in the PCS Club Disk #06, and also in Stonysoft #1729, this is the sequel to the Magnetic Pinball "table", with a bump up in action and a few surprises.

180431.overview: The final entry in the Magnetic Pinball trilogy (but possibly not the last), with this table offering more magnetism than ever before. Published in PCS Club Disk #08, and also in Stonysoft #1731.

180603.overview: Megapede is a simple Centipede clone developed by Paul Andrus and published by Skyles Electric Works in 1983. The game is all in ASCII/PETSCII characters. The horrible Megapede will twist and turn and writhe from the top of the screen to the bottom, and you must destroy it before it gets you. Oh yes, there are poisonous snails and other obstacles to watch out for, too!

180612.overview: More new levels for you Push'Em puzzlers! Also known as Mic's Push' Em.

181660.overview:
A rogue agent has broken out of a U.S. high security prison. He smuggles himself a gun boat and he is now spreading chaos and carnage across 3 different parts of the world. Sightings of the gun boat has been spotted in the docks near a city in the UK. Your mission is to send your heavy armored tank through the three different war zones, and destroy the enemy forces. Then if you can get far enough, head your way through the city to the docks and fight the spy in his stolen gun boat (and of course destroy it with him inside it). Shoot anything that shoots, collect power ups in parachutes to gain more firing ability. Have fun.

This game works on PAL machines only (or an eumulator in PAL emulation mode)

181689.overview: Monster trivia is a trivia game for up to four players. Match wits with up to 3 opponents as you attempt to answer over 2000 trivia questions in six categories (show-bizz, sports, science, history, the arts, grab bag) to determine who gets to have "lunch" with the Monster. Unlike some other trivia games from that period of time, you have to type in your answers to the exact letter. If you're wrong, the Trivia Monster screams bloodcurdlingly or tries to break the door separating you from your "lunch date".

181826.overview: Moonlight Dash 2 is a Boulder Dash game created by Boulderwilli using the Boulder Dash Construction Kit

181827.overview: Moonlight Dash 3 is a Boulder Dash game created by Boulderwilli using the Boulder Dash Construction Kit. It is a followup to Moonlight Dash 2 (there was no Moonlight Dash 1)

182986.overview:
Mario's Cement Factory is an unofficial Commodore 64 conversion of the classic Nintendo Game & Watch game of the same name. Made by hayesmaker in 2020.

Gameplay:

The player controls Mario working in a cement factory, where one has to make sure the cement carried from the top of the screen reaches one of the two concrete mixers on the lower corners of the screen safely. The cement can't go directly into the mixers though. It must first go through four tanks which Mario can open by activating levers. His task is to go back and forth between all four spots and release the concrete before anything is spilled. Failure to do so will result in dumping of said concrete on the truckers waiting to make their delivery. To reach the different levers Mario must travel between floors via elevators, which must be taken carefully to avoid Mario falling off. Game B is a harder version of the game.

Controls:

    Joystick in Port 2
    Left + Right Move Mario
    Fire to Operate Hopper Levers
    F3: In Title Screen or Game - Change border colour
    F7: Pause
    Use Keyboard to Enter a Highscore.

183790.overview: The unreleased Armalyte 2 on the C64. It is pretty much just a sprite swap of the main ship as the level itself is from the original Armalyte. The sequel was to have been programmed by the immaculate Cyberdyne Systems, a few ideas were placed. The main ship was to be more colourful, the aliens more intelligent and a power-up shop was to be included too. It was to borrow more from Salamander too! The game was to feature around 6 levels in total, and just the one player to fit in all the improvements. Flickering problems from the first game were to be removed and other various improvements. Unfortunatly, Cyberdyne Systems were contracted out to System 3, and after getting to work on projects for System 3, such as Deadlock and Last Ninja 3. Armalyte 2 was shelved.

187354.overview:
Mr. Break-Thru is a standard Breakout clone developed by David M. Moorman and published by J & F Publishing, in Loadstar #183.

The game supports both joystick and mouse.

187591.overview:
Miss Milligan is a patience game which is played using two decks of playing cards. According to Peter Arnold, author of Card Games for One, this classic game's enduring popularity is in part due to its amazing tendency to enable complete recovery from seemingly hopeless positions.

Rules:

First, eight cards are dealt in a row; they are bases for eight columns in the game. Any ace that becomes available is put onto the foundations, to be built up by suit. Other cards are built down by alternating color. One card can be moved at a time, although a sequence can also be moved in part or in whole as one unit. When an empty column occurs, only a King or a sequence starting with a King can be placed on it.

When no more moves can be made, a new set of eight cards is dealt, each for every column, whether full or empty. Then the game resumes until all possible moves are exhausted, after which a new set of eight cards is placed. This cycle of dealing new cards and making moves continues until the stock is exhausted.

After the stock has run out, there is no redeal. However, there is special move called either "waiving" or "weaving". The player can pick up a card or a sequence of cards and set it aside (this is the dominant rule; some rule sets state that only one card can be picked up). The card or sequence can later be placed back on to the tableau at any time as long as it can be built legally. Only one card or sequence of cards can be set aside at a time. Computerized solitaire applications that feature this game include a reserve cell for this purpose.

The game ends when no more useful moves can be made. The game is won if all cards are built onto the foundations. 

The C64 version was written by Maurice Jones and published by J & F Publishing in Loadstar #167 in 1998.

191268.overview: Figures + Formulas, a computing encyclopedia of weights and measures, lets the whole family calculate, convert and compare. Figures + Formulas helps children understand how and why measurement systems work by letting them calculate almost anything -big and small numbers, the serious and the silly- in an entertaining format. Quizzes are included for practical reinforcement of math skills.

192075.overview:
Your typical macho game. First enter how many there are in the Jury, then their names. Now you can judge face, boobs, overall appearance
and the computer will calculate the winner based on your ratings... 
 
Miss All Bare America: Every year in the U.S. they elect the Miss All Bare America. You usually see tiny excerpts in cinema or on your video.
But Computer freaks - now your C-64 makes it possible: You and your party-guests are members of the jury to vote who of the 40 prettiest girls will win the com- petition who will be the Miss All Bare America. A disc full of superb graphics showing dream girls you'll love

192348.overview: Math Magic is a series of tutorial-style educational software. It teaches your children the basics of addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division of whole numbers, decimals and fractions.

192349.overview: A casino gambling game released by Bug-Byte and in Italy's Go Games n.15 (December 1986) and in Alga Soft n.2b.

192706.overview: Matchmaker World Geography is a new curriculum-based learning program that has been teacher designed to develop and strengthen knowledge of geographic facts. It will support most global geography courses taught in schools. The program is versatile and easy to use. It requires no previous computer background. Matchmaker World Geography works on the principle of matching words and phrases. It is excellent for expanding and reinforcing factual knowledge of global geography. Matchmaker World Geography also has a unique authoring feature which lets you create your own programs, quizzes and games simply by typing your entries on the computer keyboard.

192728.overview: Matchmaker Elementary Science Facts is a new curriculum-based learning program that has been teacher designed to develop and strengthen knowledge of Grade 5 and 6 science facts. It will support most science courses taught in schools.

192732.overview: Matchmaker Grammar is a new curriculum-based learning program that has been teacher designed to develop and strengthen basic grammar and word use skills. The program is versatile and easy to use. It requires no previous computer background. Matchmaker Grammar works on the principle of choosing the correct grammatical form of words used in sentences. It has been developed to expand and reinforce learning of grammar skills Grades 4, 5 and 6. In a challenging game format, with colorful graphics and positive feedback to reinforce learning and assure success, Matchmaker Grammar is motivating, fun and educationally rewarding.

193470.overview: Mini-Tris is a simple single player Tetris clone with simple graphics developed by Waldemar Schott and published by Markt & Technik in 64'er 1990/08.

193584.overview: Fidgits Music School is an educational music game for children. It was developed by Walter E. Meyers and published in Ahoy! 1986/07 (Issue #31).

194308.overview:
Marble Logic is a puzzle game in which you have to match three or more (Match 3) colors to remove them. The bars to the left and right must be increased to the top so that you get to the next stage.

The game was heavily inspired by games like Bejeweled. This was developed by Peter Chlud and released for free in 2006.

194310.overview: Mars Buggy is a clone of Moon Patrol developed by Vahid Azodi and published by Business Press International in Your Computer 1985/02. If you have not seen the game in the arcades here is a brief description. You control a buggy which can  jump and fire bullets in horizontal and vertical directions. The game is played on a scrolling screen which scrolls from right to left you have three lives at the beginning of the game and one life is deducted every time you fall into a ditch or hit a rock or get hit by a bullet from the space ships. The object of the game is to stay alive as long as possible.

194577.overview: Destroy the killer Mozzies before they get you, they'll suck your blood out for sure! Published as part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack".

194613.overview: An overhead racing game and part of the "C64/128 Battle Pack". Mayhem on the freeway.

196062.overview: Melissa is an Italian language text adventure\RPG with selectable answers published in both Commodore 64 Club #01 [Italian Release], and in Commodore 64 Club #09 [Italian Release].

196121.overview: An Italian Language text adventure with "Hi-Res" graphics released in both Commodore 64 Club #02 [Italian Release], and in Commodore 64 Club #08 [Italian Release].

196676.overview: The Most and the Least is an educational quiz game developed by Orson Scott Card (Yes THAT Orson Scott Card) for the C64. It was published as a type in by Ion International in Ahoy! 1986/03 (Issue #27)

197794.overview:
Mega Fun is a 2004 Australian C64 game cartridge release that is actually a collection of three games that were never officially released outside of North America. They were all games that were originally published as type-in games from the North American based Ahoy! magazine

They are:


-     Tenpins (called Tenpin Bowling on the menu screen): a basic, but fun horizontal bowling game

-     Meteor Run (called Meteor Runner on the menu screen): A side scrolling shooter in which you have to shoot meteors coming toward you 

-     Vortex (a shooter in which you have to shoot and destroy a space station surrounded by a forcefield)

Two of the three games were developed by Tony Brantner, while Vortex was developed by Sean D. Wagle.

198078.overview:
A Day in the life of our mega-star.
 
Find all your friends so they can come to your rave.
 
Good luck!
Published by Champion Software and in Italy as Mister Egg in Tutto C64 n.2 (1992/1993).

198430.overview: Multiplication Tic Tac Toe is a math based Tic Tac Toe game that revolves around multiplication. It is a conversion of an old Commodore Plus/4 game. The conversion was done by Barry "Cout" Hart in 2017.

198806.overview: A simple shooter with pseudo-vector graphics. Protect the moon from the invading alien spacecraft. Developed by Anders Persson and released in 1988.

198813.overview:
No to be confused with the ZX Spectrum game of the same name, this game is a vertically scrolling shooter developed by C.P. and J.J. Gosoen using Chris Yates' Shoot 'em Up Construction Kit.  It was released into the public domain in 1988. In Italy, it was released under the name Bruffer in Special C64 n.4 (1991/1992) and as Cingo in Special Program n.92 (dicembre 1992). 
 
ON the moon of Cingo 12 of the XMT 125484 galaxy, the longest and most horrible war in recorded history is taking place. You are a solider of the Green army and with your tracked vehicle you are able to venture inside enemy lines to destroy as many of the enemy as possible. Use your protonic cannon and avoid as many enemy shots as you can. Beware, their goal is to annihilate you!

199208.overview:
Miner is a game with some resemblance to Boulder Dash, but also has a unique spin on the genre. You start off at the top of the screen, underneath a building of some sorts. Your goal is to dig through the screen finding gold along the way. Unlike Boulder Dash however, boulders cannot crush you, but you can use them to trap enemies that actually can kill you. Collect as much gold as you can and return it to the building once there is enough gold in the building it's onto the next screen.

Miner was developed by Gus Vakalis and published as a type-in listing in COMPUTE!'s Gazette 1991/07 which was an insert in the Compute Magazine.

199216.overview: Mad Race is a horizontal timed racing game. See how far you can get before you run out of energy. The game was developed by Sputnik World and released into the public domain in 2018

199429.overview:
Not to be confused with Maze-Man from CP Verlag, which is a Pac-Man style game. This game is actually a computerized version of the popular pen and paper maze escape games. Escape the maze within in certain time period to try to beat the time of the last player (or your own last score). Pressing the fire button draws a new maze.

This was developed by Victor Terrana and published in Loadstar #74.

199624.overview: A space shooter with a twist: instead of the usual fare of invading aliens or hostile ships, you face off against actual planets, complete with projectile moons and a chip on their shoulder. As each attack wave begins, the pissed-off celestial bodies zoom in from afar, brandish their orbiting moons, and try to hurl them at your ship. Planets are protected against your shots, until all their moons are destroyed; at this point, they go mad (visible as a bright orange glow) and attempt to ram you to death. Published in Italy in COM 64 n.13/bis (maggio 1986) and in Europe in Commodore Zone Issue #13.

199627.overview: Playing a bit like Bubble Bobble, for me, Mad Springs is a good take on that arcade classic and recommended. Published in Germany in both Magic Disk 64 1991/03, and in Game On GE 1992/2. Published in Italy as Trainer in both Hit Parade C64 n.60 (Ottobre 1991) and New Special PlayGames n.43 (giugno 1991).

199631.overview: Mc Rat (or McRat as it's sometimes spelled) is cutsey single-screen platformer for the Commodore 64. It was developed by Michael Svendsen and published in Loadstar #169.

199633.overview: In this unauthorized conversion of the 1983 Spectrum version done by Stefan Wessels that was at the time authored by Matthew Smith you play the role of Miner Willy, a bold explorer and adventurer. He discovers a network of underground caverns used by an advanced but now extinct civilization, and realizes that the mines contain lucrative metal ores. Through 20 caverns, you must collect all treasures before all time (air) runs out, watching out for the nasty guardians, the obstacles, dead falls, quicksands and all elements to be found in a classic platform game

199637.overview: A brain/memory game for 1 to 10 people created by James Midgley & John van Ness and published by Micro Spec and by Suncom as part of the "Suncom Six Pack Plus". Published in Italy in Computing videoteca Nuova serie - Giochi Di Società 2 (giugno 1986).

200256.overview: Psytronik Software is proud to present a fantastic new PREQUEL to the legendary classic release Miner 2049er - a brand-new C64 release by Daniel Avery! Produced with permission and support from the original game author Bill Hogue, the game reproduces the look and feel of the original game. Miner 2019er features 14 all-new levels along with ports of three Colecovision exclusive levels - now available on the C64 for the first time ever! The game also introduces several new elements such as hidden items, bonus levels, speed medals and more!

200344.overview:
You awake tied to chair in a large room which looks part of a large mansion. You have a sore head and no memory. You know that you need to get out of this place. As you explore the mansion your memory slowly comes back to you and you realise you were involved in a robbery. The thieves for some reason have left the loot and hidden it about the house. You now want to find the treasure before making your escape.

Million Dollar Jewel Heist is a text-only adventure where you type in your commands via the keyboard. Each screen describes your location and allows you to type in your commands.

200575.overview:
Infocom released Zork 1, 2 and 3 in the early 80s. They were all made to be playable on the home computers of the day using a disk drive.

As some of you are aware, they also created a cut-down version of Zork 1, called Mini-Zork 1, which was just small enough to fit into memory on a C64, so that it could be distributed on tape. This game was sold for a while in the UK, and possibly in some other markets. It was also included on a cover-tape with the C64 magazine Zzap! 64 in 1990.

A lesser known fact is that they created Mini-Zork 2 as well, a cut-down version or Zork 2, small enough to fit in the memory of a C64. For one reason or another, they abandonded the project when it was sort-of-completed and mostly working.

30+ years later, the source code of all their games emerged, including this project. Torbjörn Andersson has put in the work to fix all bugs he could find in this game. Before he started, it definitely wasn’t possible to play the game to completion. Now it is.

200821.overview:
Mount St. Helens is a choose your own adventure type game. The catch is that there's only one right choice for every action.

The game places you on the slopes of Mount St. Helens during a volcanic eruption. The goal is to get to safety. At every turn the game describes the scenario and offers some options. The player simply types the number of the option he or she wants to perform. Picking the wrong one will result in an untimely death.

201068.overview:
Brought into existence through human misadventure, four gigantic beasts have emerged to duke it out toe-to-toe in an epic brawl across the continents!

Take control of the monster of your choice and battle against the AI or another player in this furiously-paced PESTCII party-puncher! Who will be hailed as the King of Monstros in the Monstro Giganto hall of fame?!

Developed by Antonio Savona, Lobo and Aldo Chiummo of the Pirates of Zanzibar, Monstro Giganto is a one or two player brawler of epic sized proportions! Featuring relentless arcade style gameplay, huge and highly animated player characters, 101% PETSCII graphics, over 250 words of digitised speech (your Commodore 64 has never been this chatty!), a killer sound track, on-cartridge high score saving, unlockables and full PAL/NTSC compatibility, Monstro Giganto is a game worth fighting over!

202124.overview:
Guide Rodwina around the maze, collecting the dots. Not forgetting to collect bombs and use them to blow up Rodwina's enemies: Linda La Hughes, Growbags Grotbags, Bob (Kate), Tubbs Tattsyrup & Uncle Quentin. 

Along with tweaked graphics, Ms Rodmän has three new levels. Each level has three screens: Garden, House & Basement - Nine unique screens.

202164.overview:
You'd think it was a "minesweeper" game by the title but its really a fast-paced and really tough shooter. Released as Strasdenian in Italy in International Games n.8 (settembre 1991).  
 
You are on patrol in the skies of Frekkel orbital station when aliens are spotted approaching. Thus begins your battle against the strange and menacing beings who want to conquer the world. You must fly (being careful not to hit the buildings) and destroy the aliens that appear on your dial with your laser cannon. You have to be very careful as they are very fast and often have unpredictable movements. At the end of the squadron of enemies you will have to face the Strasdenian support ship which is very powerful and must be hit many times to destroy. If you can get past the support ship make your way to a tougher level with a mothership at the end.

203381.overview:
A spaceship is on a mission: it flies over enemy bases and is subjected to fire from the base and must avoid flying objects, for impact with them can destroy your craft. The action begins in a path limited by two walls which must not be touched. you will need to be a master pilot to avoid the walls, enemy fire and craft. You have three lives to get you to the end of the challenge. 

Published in Italy as Moonbase in Logica 2000 n.90 (1989).

203478.overview:
Touted as being harder than the original Elite release. This version was released in Italy as Missione Commando in Supplementi Edigamma/pubblirome - big 100 (1987), in Special Games n.16 (settembre 1988), and in Super C64 e C128 n.21 (marzo 1988). Also released in Stonysoft #0291 / a.k.a. "Commando III".  

A vertically scrolling shooter created with the Shoot'em Up Construction Kit. Inspired by those films that tell the stories of reckless soldiers who go alone behind enemy lines with the task of creating confusion through destruction and killing. The hero must survive and kill as many of the enemy as possible. They are aided by the cover of rocks and other impediments while our hero has no such luxury.

203523.overview:
MW ULTRA is a reinterpretation of the original Metal Warrior game released in 1999 that sees you take control of Ian as he unravels a conspiracy taking place around him and inside his mind. Ian will have to use his wits and his skills to survive against street gangs, highly trained soldiers, wild animals, robot drones and much more as you navigate your way though many different environments in order to uncover the truth to who he really is.

MW ULTRA is a great title that features interactive action adventure gameplay all within the confines of an engrossing story environment. In asking him what inspired him to reboot the Metal Warrior Series after its long hiatus, Lasse reveals:

“Each of the original MW games had been made in an ad-hoc manner based on the ideas I had at the moment, both for story and gameplay. Combined with that I was still only learning programming, game design and storytelling, particularly with the first game, this left the feeling that things could have been done better.”

Indeed it is perhaps a little known fact that Lasse experimented to reboot the franchise for the Game Boy Advance and PC but these turned out to be failed attempts that fizzled out to nothing. It wasn’t until a co-worker (Marja Kuipers) began writing fan fiction based on Lasse’s trilogy of novels that featured Metal Warrior characters that firmly planted the seed that a reboot of the series would be warranted in an expanded story setting.

205097.overview:
Merge 64 is a puzzle game by Nick "Arlasoft" Sherman, with music and SFX by Richard Bayliss. It is based on a mobile game called Shoot 'n' Merge, which itself is loosely based on 2048. 

The blocks continually scroll from right to left. You can move your block on the left to any path you like, and then press fire to launch it down the path. If it stops next to a block or blocks containing the same number, they will merge to create a block of double value. Each extra block merged doubles the value further, and newly merged or moved blocks can also combine with blocks next to them to create long chain-reactions. The game ends when any of the blocks reach the left-hand side.

205238.overview: A vampire themed text adventure by Paul Allen Panks. While it's technically public domain, it was also released on one of the later issues of Loadstar, which was Loadstar #238 in 2003.

205671.overview:
Take the role of Koji Kabuto, the pilot of 70's classic anime super-robot Mazinger Z in his quest to save Japan from the mechanical monsters created by evil scientist Doctor Hell. 

Mazinger Z was designed by Doctor Kabuto (Koji's grandfather) using state-of-the-art technology (Z-Alloy and Photonic Energy) in Japan's national Photonic Research Institute near mount Fuji. These hearquarters along Japan main cities have become the main targets for Dr. Hell's army...

205846.overview:
Mario - Die unheimliche Mine is a Text Adventure game with Graphics, published by 64'er, which was released in 1985. Specifically this was released in both 64'er Sonderheft 1985/02 and in 64'er Sonderheft 52. This game was later translated (unofficially) into English, though still with the German title.

The story is a persiflage of the first two Lord of the Rings books.

206572.overview:
Monster Catcher is a fast action, single player game for the Commodore 64! If you like Rodland, Bubble Bobble, and a little bit of Smash TV then you’ll love Monster Catcher!

Monsters have invaded, and the bunnies are in trouble! Grab your magic wand and use your capture spell to save the day! But careful you don't trap a bunny by mistake!

•    Randomly generated levels
•    40 levels plus an end game boss
•    4 different areas
•    9 different enemies with lots of varied behaviours
•    4 different power ups: lightning bolt, magic boost, shield, and extra life.

206929.overview:
